papers.title: WAIT-A-SEC: A Human-Centered Design Approach to Privacy Communication for Social Media Oversharing
papers.abstract: Social media platforms often operate on extractive security logics that prioritize frictionless data sharing, leaving users disempowered and prone to oversharing sensitive information, without fully recognizing the associated privacy implications. We present WAIT-A-SEC (Warnings About Information Transfer And Sharing: Encouraging Caution), hereafter referred to as WAITASEC, an interactive proof-of-concept prototype that delivers real-time privacy alerts while users compose posts to minimize instances of oversharing. Leveraging a synthetic dataset of 90 annotated examples of realistic user-generated content, our evaluations compare three separate models 1) a rule-based regular expressions (regex) and named entity recognition (NER) through spaCy, 2) a large language model (LLM) and 3) a hybrid model that combines the previous two models as well as incorporates a knowledge graph (KG) and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to provide context. In this hybrid approach, regex and NER yield candidate classifications, which are then validated and expanded by the LLM, utilizing RAG to retrieve relevant context from the KG before sending feedback back to the user. This classifier achieves optimal performance (Macro-F1 = 0.897; Micro-F1 = 0.834), significantly reducing critical false negatives. Grounded in Technical and Professional Communication (TPC) and active learning principles, we advocate for a warning-first design that introduces intentional pedagogical friction. This tactical approach promotes user reflection and fosters enduring privacy literacy, restoring user agency rather than relying on passive, automated redaction. This paper concludes with deployment considerations and next steps for user studies.

papers.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and validation of the gameful experience scale (GAMEX) for Brazil
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Gamification has emerged as an innovative teaching methodology, particularly in nursing education, fostering engagement and active learning. Objective To translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Gameful Experience Scale (GAMEX) for Brazilian Portuguese. Methods A methodological, quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted in three phases: linguistic and cultural adaptation, content validation, and construct validation. The cross-cultural adaptation followed World Health Organization guidance and the six-stage process described by Beaton et al.: forward translation, synthesis, back translation, expert committee review, pre-testing, and documentation of the final version. Content equivalence was assessed through expert committee review and pre-testing with representatives of the target population. Construct validity was examined using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with a diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS) estimator and polychoric correlations, and reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega. Discriminant validity was examined using the average variance extracted (AVE), the Fornell-Larcker criterion, and the heterotrait-monotrait ratio (HTMT). Results A total of 135 participants were included in the validation sample, with a mean age of 30.1 ± 13.1 years (range: 17–67 years). The sample comprised 82 students (60.7%) and 53 professionals (39.3%) from the nursing school setting. The Brazilian Portuguese adaptation demonstrated promising psychometric performance. Domain reliability levels were as follows: Enjoyment (α = 0.911; ω = 0.910), Absorption (α = 0.917; ω = 0.917), Creative Thinking (α = 0.866; ω = 0.869), Activation (α = 0.657; ω = 0.556), Absence of Negative Affect (α = 0.852; ω = 0.856), and Dominance (α = 0.770; ω = 0.770). CFA supported the overall six-factor structure, with χ² = 581.706, df = 309, χ²/df = 1.883, CFI = 0.958, TLI = 0.953, RMSEA = 0.081 (90% CI: 0.071–0.091), and SRMR = 0.102. However, RMSEA and SRMR were marginally above the prespecified thresholds, and the Activation domain showed weaker psychometric performance. Items Q18 and Q19 require further linguistic, experiential, and psychometric refinement. Conclusions The Brazilian Portuguese adaptation of GAMEX showed promising evidence of structural validity and internal consistency for assessing gamified learning experiences, such as escape rooms, in this nursing education sample.

papers.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Finite Element Operator Network for Solving Non-Smooth PDEs
papers.abstract: Abstract. We introduce the Discontinuous Galerkin Finite Element Operator Network (DG–FEONet), a data-free operator learning framework that combines the strengths of the discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method with neural networks to solve parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) with discontinuous coefficients and non-smooth solutions. Unlike traditional operator learning models such as DeepONet and Fourier Neural Operator, which require large paired datasets and often struggle near sharp features, our approach minimizes the residual of a DG-based weak formulation using the symmetric interior penalty Galerkin (SIPG) scheme. DG-FEONet predicts elementwise solution coefficients via a neural network, enabling data-free training without the need for precomputed input-output pairs. We provide theoretical justification through convergence analysis and validate the model’s performance on a series of one- and two-dimensional PDE problems, demonstrating accurate resolution of discontinuous coefficients, sharp features, and interface-induced non-smoothness, strong generalization across parameter space, and reliable convergence rates. Our results highlight the potential of combining local discretization schemes with machine learning to achieve robust, non-smooth-feature-aware operator approximation in challenging PDE settings.

papers.title: Risk factors for revisions in patients following total hip arthroplasty and hemiarthroplasty due to femoral neck fractures
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and hemiarthroplasty (HA) are established treatments for displaced femoral neck fractures (FNF), yet factors associated with revision following either procedure remain poorly defined. This study evaluated demographic, clinical, and laboratory predictors of revision after THA and HA for FNF. Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a tertiary trauma centre including 2,522 patients treated with arthroplasty for FNF (885 THA, 1,637 HA). Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and pre- and postoperative laboratory parameters were compared between patients who underwent revision and those who did not. Variables significant on univariate analysis were entered into multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to determine optimal cutoff values for significant continuous predictors. Results Revision occurred in 93 of 885 THA patients (10.5%) and 43 of 1,637 HA patients (2.6%) ( p < 0.001). In the THA cohort, patients requiring revision were younger (65.4 vs. 72.5 years, p < 0.001), had shorter hospital stays (5.4 vs. 7.5 days, p = 0.001), higher postoperative haemoglobin (10.5 vs. 9.6 g/dL, p < 0.001), and lower postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (10.8 vs. 15.7 mg/dL, p = 0.007). Multivariable analysis identified younger age (OR 0.94 per year, 95% CI 0.91–0.98; p = 0.003), higher postoperative haemoglobin (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.01–1.66; p = 0.044), and lower postoperative CRP (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.90–0.99; p = 0.029) as independent predictors of revision. ROC analysis identified age < 60 years (AUC 0.66) and postoperative haemoglobin ≥ 10.55 g/dL (AUC 0.63) as optimal thresholds. In the HA cohort, only postoperative lymphocyte count differed significantly between revision and non-revision groups, precluding multivariable analysis. Conclusions Revision following arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture was substantially more common after THA than HA. Among THA patients, revision was associated with younger age and markers of better postoperative physiological recovery rather than medical frailty. These findings suggest that revision risk after fracture-related THA may largely reflect the greater activity level and longer survivorship of healthier patients, information that may assist preoperative counseling and individualized procedure selection.

papers.title: Technical Feasibility of an Ex Vivo Bovine Trabecular Bone-Titanium Implant Co-Culture Platform for Early Interface Studies
papers.abstract: Ex vivo bone organ cultures may bridge the gap between simplified in vitro systems and animal studies. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the technical feasibility of a bovine trabecular bone–implant co-culture platform over 21 days. Thirty-two bone cylinders from three donors were cultured with porous Ti6Al4V implants. A central 6 mm channel reduced the maximum theoretical radial diffusion distance to approximately 2.5 mm. Wurtzite and diamond architectures were coupled to experimental run and femoral laterality, precluding independent evaluation of architecture-dependent biological effects. Constructs received no load, sustained static load, or static load combined with daily or weekly dynamic compression at 1 Hz for 300 cycles per session. Loaded assemblies comprised four constructs beneath a shared plate; individual forces, stresses, and strains were neither measured nor independently controlled. Metabolic activity, viability, histology, bone volume fraction, immunofluorescence, and implant colonization were assessed. Structural comparisons were cross-sectional. Metabolic activity initially decreased before increasing from day 7 onward, and viable cells and extensive implant colonization were observed after 21 days. No loading-dependent biological or structural differences were detected. The findings support technical feasibility but do not establish mechanobiological sensitivity. Further validation requires specimen-specific mechanical monitoring, re-optimization of loading parameters, and quantitative biological endpoints.

papers.title: Translational advances in smart sensor-integrated 3D bioprinting for tracheal tissue engineering
papers.abstract: Since the trachea has complex anatomical, mechanical, and biological needs, tracheal problems caused by congenital defects, injuries, prolonged intubation, infections, and cancer still pose major clinical problems. The trachea should be able to keep an open airway, possess a functional respiratory epithelium that is able to perform mucociliary clearance, and also be flexible during breathing and neck movements. Nonetheless, limited availability of donors, immune rejection, infections, restenosis, mechanical misfits, and long-term failures are all problems that hinder the current clinical treatments such as autografts, allografts, and synthetic stents. Therefore, tracheal regeneration remains a problem. This review shows how 3D bioprinting with the use of biosensing technologies, which include biosensors to measure oxygen concentration, pH level, mechanical strain, and tissue maturation in real-time, allows creating smart tracheal tissues. Alongside with the methods of extrusion bioprinting, stereolithography, multimaterial bioprinting, and hybrid bioprinting, the mentioned approaches allow recreating the complex structure of the trachea, its biomechanical gradient, and microenvironment of the trachea. This advancement in 3D bioprinting results in designing smart and functional tracheal grafts that can respond to the changing biological environment. Nevertheless, there are many translational obstacles, which include airway patency, mechanical stability, biocompatibility, and biosensor reliability among others. The integration of biosensors ensures the monitoring of cellular activity, scaffold behavior, and tissue development, which helps in designing the printing techniques. This review paper emphasizes the developments in 3D bioprinting, smart biosensing, digital twin, and artificial intelligence used for tracheal regeneration. Such integrated technology helps in the transformation of experimental products to clinical products of higher quality and intelligence.

papers.title: Stiffness-to-weight optimization of parametric lattices via adaptive voxelization and genetic algorithms
papers.abstract: This paper presents a fully automated and intelligent methodology for designing, modeling, and optimizing lattice-based materials tailored for MEX additive manufacturing. The proposed approach is based on a parametric design of a stiffened rhomboidal lattice derived from a modified octahedral unit cell, engineered to enhance mechanical performance under uniaxial compression while ensuring support-free printability. The geometry is governed by a compact set of parameters and a manufacturability constraint (α). A fast and efficient analytical model, rooted in beam theory and the stiffness method, replaces conventional FEA to predict mechanical behavior with high accuracy. This model feeds a genetic algorithm that optimizes the stiffness-to-weight ratio within the internal volume of the part. A voxelization system, adaptive to local stress fields, enables intelligent geometry adjustment, avoiding manual modeling or costly topology optimization. The methodology was validated through simulations and ASTM D695-15 compression tests, with relative errors below 5%. Results revealed the influence of lattice density and aspect ratio on failure modes, ranging from brittle delamination to ductile deformation. A real-world case study confirmed the approach’s effectiveness, achieving material savings while maintaining structural integrity. This methodology applies to any unidirectional-element lattice typology, eliminating the need for expensive commercial software

papers.title: Catastrophic acetabular wear following polyethylene liner dissociation with locking-tab damage after total hip arthroplasty: a case report
papers.abstract: Background Polyethylene liner dissociation is an uncommon but potentially severe complication of total hip arthroplasty (THA). Loss of the intended bearing interface can permit direct femoral-head–acetabular-shell articulation, with progressive shell wear, metallic debris deposition, and acetabular bone loss. Case presentation A 73-year-old woman developed left hip pain after an accidental sprain in February 2025, having reported no hip-related symptoms after primary THA in 2020. The index Mindray implants included a 48-mm acetabular shell, a highly cross-linked polyethylene liner, a 28-mm femoral head, and a size-10 stem. Radiographs and CT with three-dimensional volume-rendered reconstruction were used to assess acetabular bone loss, classified as Paprosky type IIA. Revision revealed polyethylene liner dissociation, catastrophic shell wear-through, extensive black metallic debris deposition, and a well-fixed femoral stem. Partial locking-tab damage was identified on gross inspection, but formal retrieval analysis was not performed. Acetabular revision with iliac-crest autografting was performed while retaining the femoral stem. At 6 months, the Harris Hip Score improved from 46 to 82, and radiographs showed a stable acetabular component with evidence of graft incorporation. Conclusion This case illustrates the potential for clinically occult progression from liner dissociation to catastrophic head-on-shell wear. Gross locking-tab damage did not establish the initiating failure mechanism. Component-preserving acetabular revision was associated with a favorable short-term clinical and radiographic outcome in this patient.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation Research of Digital Twin Model of Knife Gate Based on Finite Element Analysis Under Temperature Rise
papers.abstract: Knife gate valves are widely used in industrial systems for regulating the flow of liquids, gases, and slurries under demanding operating conditions. Continuous exposure to elevated temperatures can cause thermal expansion, material degradation, stress accumulation, and structural deformation, reducing valve performance and increasing failure risk. This study proposes a Digital Twin-based thermo-mechanical performance evaluation framework integrated with finite element analysis (FEA) for knife gate valves under progressive thermal loading. Five operating temperature cases of 50∘C, 100∘C, 150∘C, 200∘C, and 250∘C were evaluated to characterize temperature distribution, heat flow, temperature-dependent yield strength, thermal and mechanical stress, deformation, safety factor, actuator torque, and seal pressure. The results demonstrate progressive thermo-mechanical degradation with increasing temperature. At 250∘C, the maximum induced stress reaches 246.45 MPa, exceeding the temperature-dependent yield strength of 235.2 MPa, while the safety factor decreases to 0.95 and deformation increases to 0.80682 mm. The required actuator torque increases to 1414.56 Nm, accompanied by a reduction in seal pressure to 1.069 MPa, a decline in valve health score from 100% to 55%, and a reduction in remaining useful life from 74.57 to 24.14 years. The Digital Twin consequently identifies the highest-temperature condition as a warning state, indicating increased structural and operational risk. The primary contribution of this work is the simultaneous prediction of stress, deformation, safety factor, torque, and remaining useful life within a single unified Digital Twin–FEA model.

papers.title: Do hydrophilic implant surfaces provide a clinically meaningful advantage?
papers.abstract: Abstract A Commentary on Vílchez B, Caneiro L, Lima C, Sanz-Sánchez I, Montero E, Figuero E, Blanco J, Sanz M Clinical and radiographic performance of two distinct sandblasted, large-grit, acid-etched implant surfaces: A split-mouth randomized clinical trial. Clin Oral Implants Res. 2026;37:141-54. https://doi.org/10.1111/clr.70071 . Question Among adults requiring bilateral implant-supported restorations in healed posterior sites, does a chemically modified hydrophilic sandblasted, large-grit, acid-etched (SLActive) implant surface provide superior peri-implant tissue outcomes compared with a conventional SLA surface after one year of functional loading? Design Multicentre, split-mouth, randomized controlled clinical trial with blinded outcome assessment and 1-year follow-up after prosthetic loading. Case selection Adults (≥18 years) requiring at least two implants in healed posterior ridges located in different quadrants were recruited from two university referral centers in Spain. Eligible sites had healed for at least 3 months after extraction and required neither simultaneous hard- nor soft-tissue augmentation. Exclusion criteria included uncontrolled systemic conditions affecting healing, poor oral hygiene (full-mouth plaque score ≥20%), heavy smoking (>10 cigarettes/day), pregnancy, untreated periodontal disease, severe parafunctional habits, insufficient keratinized mucosa (<2 mm), recent grafting procedures, or other local or systemic factors that could compromise osseointegration. Seventy patients were screened; 68 were randomized, each receiving one SLActive implant and one conventional SLA implant according to a split-mouth allocation (136 implants total). Owing primarily to early implant failures and protocol-related exclusions inherent to the paired design, 61 participants completed follow-up, while 56 contributed complete radiographic data for analysis of the primary outcome. Data analysis The primary endpoint was radiographic marginal bone level (MBL) change from prosthetic loading to 12 months. Secondary outcomes comprised MBL changes from implant placement, implant stability quotient (ISQ), wound healing, peri-implant clinical parameters, implant and prosthesis survival, adverse events, and oral health-related quality of life (OHIP-14). The patient served as the unit of analysis. Quantitative variables were analysed using paired Student’s t tests and repeated-measures mixed ANOVA with Bonferroni adjustment, whereas categorical outcomes were compared using Wilcoxon or chi-square methods, with statistical significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Results Sixty-eight patients (136 implants) entered the trial and 61 completed clinical follow-up. Early implant survival before loading was 95.5% for SLActive and 97.0% for SLA implants; no additional implant losses occurred after loading (100% post-loading survival). For the primary outcome, mean MBL change from loading to 12 months was −0.04 ± 0.39 mm for SLActive implants and −0.07 ± 0.22 mm for SLA implants (mean difference 0.03 mm; 95% CI − 0.09 to 0.14; p = 0.658). A statistically significant but small difference was detected for bone remodeling from implant placement to 12 months (0.20 ± 0.39 mm vs 0.06 ± 0.20 mm; mean difference 0.15 mm; 95% CI 0.02–0.27; p = 0.024). Implant stability (baseline ISQ approximately 73; 8-week ISQ approximately 76), wound healing, probing depth (2.61 vs 2.58 mm), bleeding on probing, peri-implant mucositis prevalence, adverse events, and patient-reported outcomes were comparable between groups. No cases of peri-implantitis were observed during follow-up. Conclusions Both implant surfaces achieved excellent short-term clinical performance. Although a small statistical difference in overall bone remodeling from implant placement to 12 months favored the conventional SLA surface, no clinically meaningful superiority of the hydrophilic surface was demonstrated for the prespecified primary outcome or for clinically relevant secondary outcomes after one year of functional loading.

papers.title: Biological complications associated with aluminum ion release in implant-supported provisional restoration: a case report
papers.abstract: Implant-supported provisional restorations are widely used during the osseointegration period and may remain in contact with peri-implant tissues for extended periods. Material biocompatibility is therefore critically important. Aluminum alloys have occasionally been used for provisional frameworks due to their low cost and ease of fabrication; however, their biological safety in the oral environment remains poorly documented. This report describes a case of peri-implant osteonecrosis associated with an aluminum framework used in a provisional restoration. A 53-year-old heavy smoker with severe periodontitis received staged full-arch implant rehabilitation with a mandibular implant-supported provisional restoration using an aluminum framework. Six months later, one implant failed early with obvious sequestrum formation. A 30-day immersion test showed sustained high-level aluminum ion release from the patient’s used framework, while titanium framework released only trace levels. ICP analysis detected 18.6 µg/g aluminum in the sequestrum, markedly higher than 3.3 µg/g in normal alveolar bone. Aluminum frameworks can release considerable aluminum ions, which may represent a potential risk factor for peri-implant osteonecrosis and tissue-damage in susceptible patients. Although multiple risk factors may be involved, these findings highlight the importance of prudent material selection for provisional restorations, particularly in high-risk patients.

papers.title: Polysaccharide-conjugated nanocomposites: Synthesis, characterization, and environmental-biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Polysaccharide-conjugated nanocomposites have emerged as a pivotal class of hybrid materials, bridging natural macromolecular science with advanced coordination chemistry to address biomedical and environmental challenges. This review systematically explores the tailoring of interfaces between renewable polysaccharides such as chitosan, alginate, cellulose, starch, and pullulan and various nanoparticles, including metals, metal oxides, and carbon-based structures. In accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, a rigorous systematic search was conducted across ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar, resulting in the analysis of 182 relevant full-text articles published between 1987 and 2026. We examine the fundamental coordination mechanisms, including electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and covalent coupling, that govern the stability, morphology, and synergistic behavior of these composites. The manuscript highlights how reactive surface groups (-OH, -NH 2 , -COOH) facilitate precise structural modifications for targeted drug delivery, tissue engineering, and stimuli-responsive cargo release. Furthermore, we detail their efficacy in environmental bioremediation, specifically for heavy-metal adsorption and the photocatalytic degradation of pollutants. A significant focus is placed on green synthesis approaches and the recent integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to optimize formulation ratios and predict material performance. Advanced fabrication techniques, including 3D bioprinting and electrospinning, are discussed as pathways to enhance scalability and mimic the extracellular matrix. By addressing challenges such as nanoparticle toxicity and production costs, this review provides a roadmap for developing sustainable, next-generation functional materials within the framework of modern coordination chemistry.

papers.title: Topology-guided shell–truss transition design for additively manufactured TPMS scaffold metamaterials
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing enables complex, interconnected triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) scaffold metamaterials, but regulating their mechanical properties through relative density or wall thickness alters pore architecture and limits stiffness control at prescribed porosity. A topology-guided shell–truss transition strategy is proposed to achieve topology-assisted stiffness regulation at comparable porosity. Inspired by the morphological continuum from closed-walled through open-walled to truss-like forms in trabecular bone, topology-optimised opening patterns are introduced into closed-walled Schwarz primitive TPMS unit cells. Two representative unit-cell families, ‘D-cross’ and ‘honeycomb’, are constructed to examine how opening topology redistributes load-bearing pathways and reshapes effective stiffness. By coordinating shell thickness and feature width, the proposed metamaterials expand the Young’s modulus–density space from the single trajectory of conventional TPMS shells to a tunable region covering the trabecular-bone range. Selective laser-melted Ti6Al4V specimens confirm manufacturability and demonstrate topology-dependent differences in apparent compressive modulus and first-peak stress at nearly identical porosity. Permeability measurements confirm comparable transport performance between the topology families and trends consistent with numerical predictions. papers.title: Application of the Neumann–Monte Carlo methodology for uncertainty quantification in the bending problem of a Timoshenko beam resting on a stochastic Pasternak foundation
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes the application of the Neumann–Monte Carlo method to estimate the statistical moments of the solution to the bending problem of a Timoshenko beam resting on a stochastic Pasternak foundation. Uncertainty is modeled in the foundation’s stiffness coefficients via parameterized stochastic processes. The methodology proposed in this work differs from the usual approach, as it is developed based on theoretical results regarding the existence and uniqueness of the realizations. The consistency of the numerical approximations is ensured through rigorous analysis of the well-posedness of the underlying stochastic boundary value problem. This theoretical result guides the choice of approximation spaces via the Galerkin method, leading to realizations consistent with this result. Consequently, statistically consistent estimators of the expected value and variance of the transverse and angular displacement stochastic processes are obtained. The Monte Carlo simulation method is used to evaluate the performance of the proposed methodology.

papers.title: Survival-analysis methods for droplet-freezing data: Kaplan–Meier confidence intervals and non-parametric curve comparison
papers.abstract: Abstract. Droplet‑freezing assays underpin immersion‑mode ice‑nucleation research yet approaches to uncertainty quantification for fraction‑frozen curves and derived active‑site densities (ns(T)) are inconsistent. Further, there is not currently a rigorous method for significance testing the difference between fraction frozen curves. To address these issues, we recast droplet‑freezing measurements as survival data and apply analysis techniques typically used in medical statistics. Using the Kaplan–Meier estimator, we derive nonparametric confidence intervals for droplet fraction frozen and ns(T) without binning or model assumptions, matching Monte‑Carlo and studentized‑bootstrapped intervals on a literature volcanic ash ice nucleation dataset. Confidence intervals calculated for simulated datasets show precision improves with sample size and with steeper fraction frozen curves. Adapting the log-rank test, we introduce a method for comparing fraction frozen curves and demonstrate its application to literature and simulated droplet freezing datasets. We recommend reporting Kaplan–Meier confidence intervals on droplet freezing datasets and employing the log-rank test when comparing droplet fraction frozen curves.

papers.title: Model predictive quantum control: A modular approach for efficient and robust quantum optimal control
papers.abstract: Abstract Model predictive control (MPC) is one of the most successful modern control methods. It relies on repeatedly solving a finite-horizon optimal control problem and applying the beginning piece of the optimal input. In this paper, we develop a modular framework for improving efficiency and robustness of quantum optimal control (QOC) via MPC. We first provide a tutorial introduction to basic concepts of MPC from a QOC perspective. We then present multiple MPC schemes, ranging from simple approaches to more sophisticated schemes which admit stability guarantees. This yields a modular framework which can be used 1) to improve efficiency of open-loop QOC and 2) to improve robustness of closed-loop quantum control by incorporating feedback. We demonstrate these benefits with numerical results, where we benchmark the proposed methods against competing approaches.

papers.title: A compendium of board game-based learning models for oral pathology and microbiology education
papers.abstract: Dental education increasingly emphasizes active learning strategies that promote student engagement, knowledge retention, and critical thinking. Game based learning has emerged as a valuable pedagogical approach capable of transforming traditional learning environments into interactive educational experiences. Board game-based learning offers opportunities for collaborative learning, immediate feedback, and reinforcement of key concepts in health professions education. This paper presents a descriptive compendium of board game-based learning models developed for teaching Oral Pathology, Oral Histology, and Microbiology concepts to undergraduate dental students. A series of eight educational board games were designed to facilitate active learning among Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) students. Each game was developed based on specific learning objectives, curricular requirements, and principles of educational Game based learning. The games incorporated visual recognition, problem-solving, matching exercises, puzzle-solving, clue-based reasoning, and word construction activities. The descriptive compendium comprises eight unique game formats: Path and Ladder, Spin and Match, Wall-Ee, Jigsaw Puzzles, Patho-Connect, Who's My Pair?, The Jumble Box, and Find the Path. These models are intended to address diverse cognitive domains including knowledge recall, visual identification, analysis and application. The games are expected to promote teamwork, peer-assisted learning, and active participation while reinforcing foundational concepts in oral pathology and microbiology. Board game-based learning models represent innovative and adaptable educational resources for dental education. Their integration into undergraduate curricula may potentially enhance student motivation, engagement, and conceptual understanding while creating enjoyable learning experiences. These models align with SDG 4 - quality education.

papers.title: CARDINAL: physiology-guided directional structure and prototype learning for small-sample echocardiographic assessment
papers.abstract: Echocardiographic assessment of diastolic dysfunction from small clinical cohorts is susceptible to overfitting, unstable feature attribution, and poorly calibrated confidence estimates, limiting the clinical translation of machine learning models. This study aimed to develop and evaluate CARDINAL, a physiology-guided framework combining a dataset-specific structural prior, directional graph regularization, prototype-aligned representation learning, and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty estimation, and to assess whether it improves discrimination, calibration, and uncertainty-guided referral relative to established tabular learning models under a leakage-controlled protocol. We present CARDINAL, a physiology-guided framework that integrates four components: (i) a dataset-specific structural prior that encodes known physiological relations among clinical variables; (ii) directional graph refinement under sparsity and acyclicity penalties, serving as a regularizer and interpretability scaffold rather than as an identified causal model; (iii) prototype-aligned representation learning to enforce intra-class compactness under limited data; and (iv) Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty estimation ( \(T=30\) , dropout rate 0.20) for calibrated confidence and selective referral of borderline cases. The study cohort comprised 118 cases classified by a composite reference index as normal ( \(n=37\) ), mild ( \(n=42\) ), or severe ( \(n=39\) ). Evaluation followed a leakage-controlled protocol with a fixed stratified 70/15/15 split producing an 82-case training pool, an 18-case validation set, and an 18-case locked test set evaluated once after all modeling choices were finalized. On the locked test set, CARDINAL achieved a binary abnormal-versus-normal ROC-AUC of 0.969, AUPRC of 0.990, accuracy of 0.944, sensitivity of 0.923, specificity of 1.000, Brier score of 0.066, ECE of 0.095, and NLL of 0.223. Patient-level DeLong and McNemar tests were non-significant on this single split ( \(n=18\) ), reflecting limited statistical power rather than equivalence. Across 20 matched repeated runs, CARDINAL showed consistent stability with Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon \(p = 3.05\times10^{-5}\) versus TabPFN-tuned. Three-class confusion analysis indicated reasonable grade-level discrimination, with misclassifications occurring predominantly between adjacent grades. Ablation analysis suggested that each framework component—directional graph regularization, prototype alignment, and uncertainty calibration—contributed to overall performance. Three public datasets (UCI Heart Disease, Heart Failure Clinical Records, and MIMIC-IV) served as tabular robustness benchmarks; CARDINAL showed consistently modest numerical advantages across all four datasets. These results suggest that physiological structure, prototype learning, and uncertainty quantification can be integrated within a leakage-controlled evaluation framework. Feature importance analysis indicated that \({E/e}^\prime\) and LAVI—label-adjacent variables in the reference index—were the predominant contributors to model predictions, consistent with established cardiology guidelines. A complementary analysis excluding these label-adjacent variables preserved CARDINAL’s relative advantage (ROC-AUC 0.873 versus 0.846 for TabPFN-tuned). Uncertainty estimates may assist in identifying borderline cases for selective human review. These findings motivate prospective multi-center validation to evaluate clinical utility, transportability, and the impact of uncertainty-guided review on patient care.

papers.title: Damage Identification Under Viscoelastic Modeling Errors
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Model-based structural damage identification strategies are inherently susceptible to modeling errors, particularly when complex viscoelastic dissipation mechanisms are simplified in inverse analysis. This study proposes a Bayesian damage identification framework capable of accurately estimating damage location and severity in dynamic systems subject to viscoelastic modeling errors and uncertainties. Methods The methodology incorporates a Gaussian Process (GP) discrepancy model within a hierarchical Bayesian updating framework. To mitigate parameter non-identifiability between physical parameters and discrepancy hyperparameters, a physics-informed covariance kernel derived from random vibration theory is combined with data-informed hyperpriors constructed from frequency-domain residual signals. Sparse damage localization is achieved using a Spike-Slab prior. The framework is validated on a two-degree-of-freedom dynamic system with viscoelastic dampers modeled via internal variables, considering both undamaged and damaged structural conditions under low and high levels of modeling discrepancy (unmodeled relaxation dynamics and mass misspecification). Results Numerical results demonstrate that conventional Bayesian inversion (neglecting model discrepancy) fails under viscoelastic misspecification, producing spuriously concentrated posterior distributions, false damage indications, or missed detections. In contrast, the proposed discrepancy-aware formulation consistently provides accurate estimates of damage severity and location across all structural conditions while effectively preventing false-positive detections in the intact state. Conclusion Integrating a physics-informed Gaussian Process discrepancy term into the Bayesian updating scheme effectively captures residual energy dissipation mismatches without corrupting physical stiffness parameters. This provides a robust and reliable methodology for damage identification in the presence of viscoelastic model misspecifications.

The green supply chain management system, enhanced by a hyperparameter-optimized neural network model, demonstrates high predictive accuracy and resilience. It effectively forecasts environmental risks, energy consumption, and resource use while offering decision support for managers. papers.title: A physics-informed neural network method for an inverse source problem in a nonlinear time-fractional subdiffusion equation
papers.abstract: Abstract We study a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method for an inverse source problem associated with a nonlinear time-fractional subdiffusion equation with Caputo derivative of order α ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) {\alpha\in(0,1)} . The unknown source depends on both time and space and is identified from additional integral measurement data. Building on available well-posedness and stability results for the continuous inverse problem, we formulate a residual-based PINN approximation in which the state variable is represented by a neural network satisfying the homogeneous spatial boundary conditions, while the source is reconstructed in closed form through the analytical representation formula. Our main contribution is a rigorous error analysis of this computational framework. First, we derive a stability estimate showing that the error in the state and reconstructed source is controlled by the PDE and initial residuals, while the measurement residual is included in the PINN loss to enforce consistency with the observed integral data. Second, using Sobolev approximation results for shallow tanh networks, we quantify the approximation power of the neural ansatz in terms of the network size. Third, we relate the continuous generalization error to the discrete training loss by establishing explicit midpoint quadrature estimates. Combining these ingredients, we obtain computable a priori bounds for both the solution and source reconstruction errors, which reveal their dependence on the network width and quadrature resolution. Numerical experiments for representative examples support the theory and illustrate stable and accurate recovery across different fractional orders, discretization levels, and data perturbations. The results provide a mathematically justified scientific-computing framework for PINN-based inversion in nonlinear fractional diffusion problems.

papers.title: Chemistry Teachers’ Perceptions of Sustainable Living and Sustainable Development: A Qualitative Study
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine in depth the views of chemistry teachers working in different provinces of Turkey regarding sustainable living and sustainable development. In the research, which adopted a case study design from qualitative research methods, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 chemistry teachers selected through maximum variation sampling; the obtained data were analyzed through content analysis. As a result of the analysis, seven main themes were identified: perception of sustainability, relationship with chemistry science, integration into curriculum, encountered challenges, preferred methods, support needs, and professional roles. The findings reveal that teachers predominantly address sustainability through its environmental dimension and position chemistry science at the center of sustainability; while they consider the integration of topics into the curriculum necessary, they encounter obstacles such as curriculum density, exam-oriented focus, and insufficient student interest. It was determined that teachers prefer digital content and active learning approaches, need in-service training and digital material support, and define their roles around creating awareness and being role models. Accordingly, it is recommended that sustainability education be expanded to encompass economic and social dimensions, and that teachers be supported through in-service training.

papers.title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

papers.title: Thayer-inspired teaching routines as active learning in higher business education
papers.abstract: This paper reports an embedded case study of a Thayer-inspired teaching routine (M1–M2–M3) implemented across four business curricular units (covering global competitiveness, strategic marketing, international marketing, and B2B marketing) during the 2025–2026 academic year. The routine operationalises (M1) a 10–20 minutes conceptual framing with explicit learning outcomes; (M2) small-group (≤3 students) applied problem work using permitted digital tools (including AI under disclosure and verification rules); and (M3) an unsupported oral defence (no slides, notes, or devices), with mandatory individual contribution and structured questioning. Drawing on evidence on active learning effectiveness and constructive alignment, the M1–M2–M3 routine is conceptualised as integrity-by-design: students may use tools to learn and build artefacts (M2), while their individual understanding and reasoning are authenticated through a technology-free defence (M3). Across the four embedded units of analysis, findings report a trajectory from initial student discomfort and insufficient preparation to progressively stronger conceptual accuracy and argumentation. The paper documents the positive learning outcomes achieved and the structural challenges encountered (including anxiety, overload, and unequal academic capital) and discusses their implications for assessment design in AI-normalised environments

papers.title: Comparison of Forecasts From Neural Network and Econometric Models .
papers.abstract: This article provides a comparative analysis of the performance of neural network and econometric models in generating pseudo-out-of-sample multistep forecasts. Multistep forecasts with horizons of up to 12 months were generated for two periods: January 2024 to December 2025 and January to December 2025. The robustness of those results was additionally verified over a 48-month evaluation period from January 2022 to December 2025. The hyperparameters of the LSTM model were selected using random search and the Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization algorithm. The result indicated that, without properly tuned hyperparameters, even a complex nonlinear model provides no advantage over the simplest naive forecast. The stochastic nature of neural network training was taken into account to ensure a valid comparison and reproducibility of the results by testing the selected configurations for stability across a series of runs with different random seeds for which mean forecast errors and their standard deviations were calculated. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using MAPE, RMSE, and the aggregated GMFQI measure; the run time of the models was also compared. The results were compared with forecasts generated by classical econometric models: random walk (RW), ARIMA, and the linear trend (TS) model. The econometric forecasts were constructed using recursive and moving window forecasting. The conclusion was that, with appropriate hyperparameter tuning and control for reproducibility of results, the LSTM model can provide more accurate forecasts, primarily over longer evaluation periods. Nevertheless, simple econometric models provide comparable forecasting performance at substantially lower computational cost.

papers.title: NDO-MPC: A Robust Servo-Motor Model Predictive Position Control Method Based on Noise-Suppressed Disturbance Observer
papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) of servo motors is sensitive to parameter mismatch and load disturbance, as the prediction law relies on an accurate plant model. To address this issue, we propose a robust position MPC scheme with a noise-suppressed disturbance observer. Starting from the servo-motor dynamics, we establish a lumped disturbance model of the current and speed loops by a truncated Taylor expansion, which accounts for electrical-parameter variations, mechanical-parameter variations and load changes. The resulting disturbance model is used to reconstruct both the position-servo prediction model and the associated linear constraints. For the current and speed disturbance channels, generalized proportional–integral observers with embedded first-order filtering are designed so that the disturbance and its first derivative can be estimated with improved high-frequency noise attenuation. The estimated quantities are employed online to compensate the prediction model and to correct the constraint bounds. A constrained convex program, comprising an integrated position–speed–current cost and the corrected inequality constraints, is then solved by the Hildreth algorithm and applied to the inverter through space-vector pulse-width modulation. Comparative experiments on a surface-mounted permanent-magnet servo platform demonstrate that the proposed method improves positioning performance under parameter mismatch and load disturbance.

papers.title: Deep learning–based breast lesion classification using treatment response assessment maps with uncertainty quantification
papers.abstract: PurposeDynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) is widely used for breast cancer diagnosis due to its high sensitivity; however, limited specificity often leads to false positives and unnecessary biopsies. Treatment response assessment maps (TRAMs), derived from delayed contrast-enhanced imaging, characterize contrast accumulation and clearance and may improve diagnostic specificity.ApproachWe utilized the Advanced MRI Breast Lesions dataset from The Cancer Imaging Archive to develop deep learning–based models for breast lesion classification using both multiphase DCE-MRI and TRAM images. A 3D convolutional residual network (ResNet18) was employed for feature extraction, followed by a fully connected classifier. To assess prediction reliability, test-time augmentation was used to estimate aleatoric uncertainty. Radiomics-based models were also implemented for comparison.ResultsThe TRAM-based deep learning model achieved numerically higher area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.870 versus 0.835), sensitivity (0.848 versus 0.818), and specificity (0.823 versus 0.759) compared with DCE-MRI. Radiomics analysis showed similar trends. Uncertainty stratification demonstrated improved performance in low-uncertainty predictions for both modalities, where high-uncertainty DCE-MRI predictions showed a marked performance decline compared with TRAM.ConclusionsThese results suggest that TRAM-based deep learning models may provide a promising complementary imaging approach for breast lesion classification. Integration of uncertainty quantification could further enhance reliability, showing the potential of this framework for improving breast cancer diagnosis.

papers.title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Audio-Visual Stimuli based Brain-Machine Interface with Safe Model Predictive Control for Robotic Arm Trajectory Tracking in Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.abstract: Abstract Achieving effective Brain–Machine Interface (BMI) control of robotic manipulators remains challenging, particularly when integrating low-bandwidth neural commands with safety-constrained robot execution. This paper presents a pilot proof-of-concept framework for BMI-driven control of a UR5 robotic arm using a switchable audio–visual EEG paradigm combined with nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). Steady-State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEP) and Auditory Steady-State Responses (ASSR) are employed as mutually exclusive BMI channels for discrete task selection, while Error-Related Potentials (ErrP) provide supervisory feedback for safety intervention. Three stimulation frequencies are mapped to predefined manipulation tasks executed along offline, pre-computed trajectories. Robot execution is evaluated under open-loop control, a nonlinear PID controller as a reference baseline, and a safe NMPC scheme. In the proposed implementation, ErrP detection triggers suppression of robot velocity within the NMPC framework, acting as a real-time safety stop. Pilot human–robot interaction experiments demonstrate the feasibility of decoding-to-execution integration and consistent trajectory execution under NMPC. The NMPC scheme achieved tracking errors in the range of 0.043–0.137 m and task completion times of 7.3 s –7.5 s while enforcing a velocity limit of 0.25 m/s. The FBCCA method yielded average classification accuracies of 93.5% (SSVEP) and 87.5% (ASSR), averaged across two participants. These findings provide preliminary evidence of system-level feasibility, rather than population-level statistical validation, and motivate future studies with larger cohorts.

papers.title: Koopman-enhanced offline reinforcement learning for robust multi-echelon inventory control under demand distribution shift
papers.abstract: Purpose Multi-echelon inventory optimization (MEIO) under demand distribution shift remains an open challenge in supply chain management. Classical rule-based policies are effective when calibrated online but cannot exploit historical data structure. This paper investigates whether a Koopman operator world model, applied as a structured latent dynamics model within an offline reinforcement learning (RL) framework, can improve the out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness of learned inventory policies and reduce temporal difference (TD)-target variance during training. Design/methodology/approach We propose Koopman-enhanced Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization (K-MEIO), a two-stage framework combining a Deep Koopman World Model (DKWM) with Implicit Q-Learning (IQL). The DKWM learns a finite-dimensional linear embedding of the multi-echelon inventory dynamics, enabling analytically tractable TD targets with 12.4% lower variance than direct next-state encoding. The Koopman-enhanced Implicit Q-Learning policy is trained entirely on simulated offline transitions calibrated from University of California, Irvine Online Retail and Rossmann Store Sales demand statistics. Ablation experiments across five expectile values, three training seeds, and three OOD stress scenarios are reported, together with full cost breakdowns. Findings Under standard evaluation, K-MEIO achieves service level 0.995 with zero capacity violations. Across three training seeds, K-MEIO achieves OOD robustness ratio 0.861 ± 0.039 under a 3× promotional demand spike and 0.882 ± 0.058 under a permanent demand mean shift, compared to 0.762 ± 0.153 and 0.842 ± 0.093 for vanilla IQL. K-MEIO shows consistently lower seed-to-seed variance, suggesting more stable training dynamics. A historically calibrated base-stock policy (Hist-BSP) outperforms all offline methods in both standard and stress evaluations. Cost breakdown confirms that K-MEIO's degradation under stress is driven entirely by stockout cost, not excess inventory. Research limitations/implications The offline dataset consists of simulated transitions calibrated using real retail demand statistics, not actual historical inventory records. The Koopman spectral radius constraint is a regularization device and does not constitute a formal stability guarantee for the true inventory system. The 12.4% variance reduction produces modest but consistent OOD robustness gains across seeds. Practical implications In supply chain contexts where promotional demand spikes or demand mean shifts are common and online policy recalibration is impractical, K-MEIO offers more stable policy behavior than vanilla IQL (seed std. ±0.039 vs. ± 0.153 in S1). A historically calibrated BSP remains a competitive offline benchmark and should be the primary comparison point. Originality/value This paper provides the first systematic evaluation of Koopman-structured TD targets for offline inventory RL under demand distribution shift, with direct measurement of TD-target variance reduction, a multi-seed robustness analysis, and a fair historically calibrated BSP baseline. The corrected mechanistic explanation clarifies that the Koopman advantage operates at training time through variance reduction, not at evaluation time through OOD encoding.

papers.title: Piranha-Based feature subset selection and constructive sequential neural networks for enhanced cardiovascular disease prediction
papers.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is one of the most common causes of death globally. Early detection of CVD and timely treatment for preventing further health complications depend on several factors. Those variables include clinical data, redundant features, and existing machine learning models or deep learning models that do not achieve reliable prediction performance. Objective The primary objective of this research work is to develop an intelligent framework for predicting cardiovascular diseases that classifies the diseases accurately, reduces feature redundancy and enhances efficiency through optimizing feature selection. Methods The proposed Piranha-Based Feature Subset Selection with Constructive Sequential Neural Network (PFSS-CSNet) framework first applies Min-Max normalization to standardize the clinical data. The PFSS algorithm employs feature subset selection to identify the most informative clinical features. In addition, Bayesian optimization is used to determine the optimal hyperparameters of CSNet. The proposed framework is evaluated using the publicly available UCI Heart Disease dataset. Results The accuracy of the proposed PFSS-CSNet framework is 99.70%, the precision estimate is 99.50%, the recall is 99.80%, the specificity assessment is 99.60%, the F1-score is 99.60%, the G-measure is 99.70%, and the AUC is evaluated as 0.997. In comparative experiments, the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing machine learning classifiers in predicting cardiovascular diseases. Conclusion The incorporation of PFSS, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, and CSNet provides a powerful and computationally efficient framework for predicting cardiovascular diseases. The proposed method achieves accurate prediction performance on the benchmark dataset and can aid clinical decision-making. Nonetheless, routine clinical adoption requires further verification using multi-center external clinical datasets.

papers.title: Local P-th Mean Stability of Stochastic Differential Equations with Infinite Memory by Contraction Mapping Principle on Strong Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: Abstract The aim of this work is to provide details how the well-known Banach’s contraction mapping principle (CMP) can be used to derive criteria for local asymptotic p -th mean stability of the trivial equilibrium of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with infinite memory, driven by standard Wiener processes on the strong Banach space $$\mathbb {M}_p$$ M p of cádlág or cáglád stochastic processes with bounded p -th moments $$\mathbb {E}[\sup _{-\infty E [ sup - ∞ < t ≤ T | X ( t ) | p ] < ∞ . First, we prove existence, uniqueness and continuity of $$L^p$$ L p -solutions to those SDEs by using CMP. Thereafter, for the investigation of local asymptotic p -th mean stability, we carry over some techniques of Burton [9] for nonrandom differential equations to the case of SDEs with infinite memory. The derived criteria strongly depend on efficient estimates of the upper Burkholder constant of Itô-type stochastic integrals. Three examples illustrate the practical applicability of our approach. The work is supplemented by a $$L^p$$ L p -error estimate of successive iterations on strong Banach spaces $$\mathbb {M}_p$$ M p . The derived criteria help to control and optimize the long-term stability behavior of stochastic integro-differential systems with memory in the uniform moment-sense (i.e., for uncertainty quantification).

papers.title: Cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance strategy for shock resilient machines with prior usage and non-constant shock magnitude
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a modified cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance (CDSPM) model that addresses the limitations of traditional cumulative shock sequential models by incorporating three realistic factors often ignored in maintenance planning: prior damage in used machines, shock dampening effects and non-constant shock magnitudes. The research seeks to provide a more practical decision-making tool for industries, particularly in developing countries, that rely heavily on fairly-used equipment exposed to complex shock environments. Design/methodology/approach The study modifies the existing CDSPM model by introducing a non-zero initial damage state (R0 > 0), a shock dampening factor αl which is defined as the proportion of shock damage absorbed by the machine. This provides a mathematical mechanism for representing the protective effect of built-in shock-resistance components. The effective shock damage transmitted to the machine is represented by 1-αl100% with 0⩽αl⩽1. This formulation distinguishes between the physical magnitude of an external shock and the actual damage transmitted to the machine. It therefore provides a theoretical basis for incorporating mechanical protection into stochastic reliability models rather than assuming that the entire shock magnitude contributes directly to cumulative damage. Also, the Gamma-distributed shock magnitudes replace the traditional exponential distribution. The modified model formulates total expected cost functions for both infinite and finite time horizons, derives optimality conditions using Lagrange optimization, and develops a comprehensive availability model. The methodology is validated through application to a used Caterpillar 320BL hydraulic excavator using empirical field data, with the algorithm implemented in Python programming language. Findings The modified CDSPM model demonstrates that accounting for prior damage and shock resistance leads to shorter, effective and more realistic maintenance intervals with lower expected maximum cost rate compared to classical models. The optimal policy recommends P* = 12 maintenance intervals with a maximum expected cost rate of 26.99 million Naira and system availability of 98.51%, whereas the classical model (assuming pristine condition) suggests P** = 14 intervals with 58.98 million Naira cost and 99.18% availability for the case study used Caterpillar excavator. The 15% reduction in intervals and significantly lower lifecycle costs confirm the fact that classical models overestimate equipment longevity and underestimate maintenance requirements for fairly-used machines. Research limitations/implications The model's parameters are estimated from a single machine type and operational context, which may limit generalizability. The assumption of a constant shock dampening factor and fixed improvement factor may not capture all operational complexities. These identified baseline conditions are essential for real-world model development. Therefore, future research should explore time-varying dampening factors, multiple failure mechanisms and application to diverse equipment types across different industrial sectors. Practical implications The modified CDSPM model provides maintenance planners with a practical tool for scheduling sequential preventive maintenance (PM) on used equipment, enabling more accurate prediction of maintenance intervals, cost optimization and availability estimation that could not have been appropriate with fixed interval PM. The approach helps reduce unplanned failures, minimize downtime and extend equipment life through evidence-based decision-making that reflects actual machine conditions. Social implications By improving cumulative damage sequential maintenance practices for fairly-used equipment, particularly in developing countries where second-hand machinery is prevalent, the model supports sustainable industrial operations, reduces resource waste and enhances productivity and workers' safety through more reliable equipment performance. This cost-effective maintenance strategy contributes to economic efficiency in resource-constrained environments. Originality/value This research presents an integrated CDSPM model that simultaneously incorporates prior damage, shock dampening and Gamma-distributed shock magnitudes. The work extends Nakagawa and Mizutani’s (2008) foundational model as a special case while providing a more realistic model for used equipment maintenance. The availability model and finite horizon optimization approach offer novel contributions to reliability engineering practice.

papers.title: Molecular/Ionic Coupling Enables a Cycling-Evolved Gradient Interphase for Durable Zinc Metal Anodes
papers.abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc batteries hold promise for energy storage, but viability is limited by the trade-off between interfacial thermodynamic stability and Zn2+ deposition kinetics. Existing strategies address solvation or electric-field regulation separately, overlooking the coupled interplay between molecular adsorption and ionic shielding and its influence on gradient interphase evolution. We establish a molecular/ionic coupling framework using NFSI as a desolvation promoter and Y3+ as an electrostatic modulator to quantitatively tune the near-interfacial environment by regulating the desolvation barrier and local electric field, thereby promoting the development of an organic/inorganic gradient SEI with an F/S-rich outer region and a ZnF2/ZnS-rich inner region. This interphase suppresses side reactions while maintaining fast Zn2+ transport. Bayesian optimization finds the optimal formulation, enabling Zn||Zn symmetric cells to cycle >2200 h, Zn||Cu half-cells to achieve 99.76% CE over 4000 cycles, and Zn||MnO2 full cells with enhanced rate and stability. This coupling strategy provides a data-guided and transferable design principle for molecular/ionic cooperative electrolyte engineering.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Compensation of Positional Error for Collaborative Robots
papers.abstract: Abstract The positional accuracy of collaborative robots is degraded by errors from multiple sources. Existing error compensation methods improve the positional accuracy, but they output deterministic predictions without uncertainty quantification (UQ), which introduces hidden risks in high-precision applications. Moreover, directly applying Bayesian approximation techniques, such as Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, to raw joint variables is further hampered by the nonlinear coupling among joints, which yields uncertainty intervals too wide to be informative and limits point-estimation accuracy. To address these problems, this paper proposed a novel framework integrating Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) with an MC dropout neural network. KPCA extracts nonlinear features from the joint space and decouples the joint variables before they enter the network, which improves the accuracy of the learned mapping. MC dropout then generates a predictive distribution of the positional error, from which a 95% confidence interval is obtained for each target. The framework was validated on an Elite EC-63 collaborative robot. The proposed method predicts both the positional error and its uncertainty. It reduces the mean absolute positional error to 0.0546 mm after compensation. The proposed method establishes a lightweight, dual-capability framework that simultaneously provides high-precision error compensation and corresponding UQ for collaborative robots.

papers.title: Multi-strategy enhanced dung beetle optimizer for reliable hyperparameter search in multimodal emotion recognition
papers.abstract: Hyperparameter selection in multimodal emotion recognition is challenging because heterogeneous and incomplete modalities can produce noisy validation responses, while configurations selected primarily for peak predictive performance may exhibit poor probability calibration, limited robustness, or unnecessary computational cost. Reliable model selection therefore requires jointly considering discrimination, probability quality, robustness to modality loss, and search efficiency under a limited evaluation budget. To address this problem, this study proposes a multi-strategy enhanced dung beetle optimizer (MSA-DBO) that combines opposition-based initialization, diversity- and remaining-budget-dependent behavioral-role allocation, stagnation-triggered bounded chaotic escape, feasibility repair, and an uncertainty-aware validation objective. The method was evaluated against six hyperparameter-search baselines across four controlled MELD-derived feature domains. MSA-DBO achieved the highest mean weighted F1 of 79.85%, exceeding standard DBO by 4.63% points while showing lower between-run variability. It also obtained the lowest Brier score of 0.146 and negative log-likelihood of 0.425, although Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization achieved a marginally lower expected calibration error. Confidence-based deferral increased selective weighted F1 to 85.31% while retaining 84.8% of predictions. Under controlled modality masking, MSA-DBO achieved the highest weighted F1 under each single-modality omission, whereas BOHB performed slightly better when two modalities were simultaneously unavailable and retained an advantage in search efficiency. Overall, the results indicate that MSA-DBO provides a reliability-oriented hyperparameter-search strategy under the present controlled MELD-derived feature-level conditions. Not applicable.

papers.title: Multi-Time-Scale Optimal Dispatch of a Drilling Microgrid with Lithium Titanate Battery Energy Storage under Impulse Loads
papers.abstract: To address the severe impulse loads during tripping operations, the insufficient ramp capability of diesel generators, and the poor adaptability of conventional lithium-ion batteries to frequent deep charge–discharge cycles in islanded drilling-well microgrids, a multi-time-scale optimal dispatch method using a lithium titanate (LTO) battery as the core energy storage unit is proposed. The three-component decomposition characteristics of drilling load (base, impulse, and auxiliary components) are first analyzed, and the suitability of LTO batteries for drilling impulse conditions is demonstrated in terms of high-rate charge/discharge, long cycle life, wide temperature range, and safety. A three-layer collaborative dispatch framework is then established, comprising day-ahead economic dispatch, intra-day model predictive control (MPC), and real-time PQ power control. The day-ahead layer optimizes diesel output and storage schedules to minimize daily operating cost; the intra-day layer updates PV forecast errors every 15 min; the real-time layer performs impulse power smoothing within 100 ms and recovers downward-drilling braking energy. Simulation based on a 50DB drilling rig well site in an oilfield shows that, with a 1.725 MW/0.424 MWh LTO storage system, the diesel power fluctuation rate is reduced by 79%, the diesel ramp rate is controlled within 50 kW/min, the recovered braking energy reaches approximately 300 kWh per well (2.5% of daily electricity consumption), and the daily operating cost of the three-layer dispatch is reduced by about 19% compared with the two-layer scheme. The results verify the engineering applicability of LTO storage for impulse load smoothing and energy recovery in drilling microgrids, and can provide a reference for the design of green power supply systems at well sites. Keywords: drilling microgrid; lithium titanate battery; impulse load smoothing; multi-time-scale dispatch; braking energy recovery; model predictive control.

papers.title: THE TWO-LAYER ENERGY MANAGEMENT AND DISPATCH MODEL FOR MICROGRID HYBRID ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS BASED ON MPC
papers.abstract: As the penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) and wind generation in microgrids continues to rise, the strong stochasticity of renewable output and load poses significant challenges to the economic operation of microgrids, while the lifetime degradation of energy storage batteries under frequent charging and discharging further inflates the whole-life-cycle cost of the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a two-layer energy management and dispatch model for microgrid hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) based on model predictive control (MPC). The upper layer is an economic dispatch layer, which minimizes the sum of the electricity purchase cost and the battery degradation cost and adopts a 48-step receding-horizon optimization to determine hourly reference plans for battery charging/discharging and grid interaction; the degradation cost is modeled as a depth-quadratic function of the half-cycle throughput and of the lifetime parameters, thereby internalizing lifetime loss into the economic objective. The lower layer is a power smoothing layer, which tracks the upper-layer reference over a 12-step short horizon and exploits the fast response of the supercapacitor to smooth the high-frequency power fluctuations induced by renewable forecasting errors. A 48-hour closed-loop simulation is carried out using real hourly data containing PV and wind generation together with a real-time price series. The results show that the upper-layer dispatch achieves peak shaving and valley filling by charging at low prices and discharging at high prices, with a correlation coefficient of −0.620 between the electricity price and the grid interaction power; the battery state of charge (SOC) operates strictly within the safe range of [10%, 90%] throughout, with zero violations. Compared with the baseline strategy that ignores degradation, the degradation-aware strategy reduces the cumulative battery throughput by 44.0%, the standard deviation of power fluctuations by 32.1%, and the total cost by 6.2%. At a 40% forecasting-error level, the lower-layer supercapacitor raises the reduction in the root-mean-square battery power ramp to 41.2%, and the smoothing benefit becomes more pronounced as the forecasting error increases. The proposed model provides a feasible hierarchical scheduling approach for the optimal operation of microgrids with HESS, balancing operational economy and storage lifetime under uncertainty.

papers.title: Innovative Learning Strategies and Students’ Academic Performance in Selected Tertiary Institutions in Anambra State, Nigeria
papers.abstract: Education in the 21st century is undergoing a significant transformation driven by rapid technological advancement, globalization, and the evolving needs of society. There is a paradigm shift toward innovative learning strategies by tertiary institutions in Nigeria because it has the potentials to promote active engagement, critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving abilities among students. The motivation for the study emanated due to educational concerns bordering on declining academic performance, limited instructional innovation and inadequate integration of educational technologies experienced in most tertiary institutions in Nigeria. The introduction of innovative learning strategies into tertiary institutions in Nigeria has been proven to be an effective alternative to conventional teaching and learning methods which will actively engage students by enhancing motivation and engagement thereby improving learning outcomes. This research work investigated how academic performance of students in selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State could be enhanced through innovative learning strategies. Specifically, the study examined how Learning Management System (LMS) enhances students’ academic performance in selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State Nigeria. The study also investigated how flipped classroom enhances students’ academic performance in selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State Nigeria. Thirdly, the study also ascertained how collaborative learning can enhance students’ academic performance in selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State Nigeria. Accordingly, the study adopted a descriptive research design using a survey method to source the needed data from the respondents. The target population of the study consists of the students of the selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State, Nigeria. Partial least square structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the hypotheses formulated to guide the study at 5% level of significance. The findings of the study revealed that Learning Management System(LMS),flipped classroom and collaborative learning significantly and positively enhance students’ academic performance in selected tertiary institutions in Anambra State Nigeria. The study recommended that tertiary institutions should engage more on the use of learning management systems for enhanced students’ engagement and academic performance. The study recommended that tertiary institutions in Nigeria should improve the quality and consistency of flipped classroom implementation by providing well-structured pre-class materials and the use of in class sessions for active learning. The study also recommended that lecturers should strengthen collaborative learning by designing structured and assessable group activities that ensures equal participation, accountability and interaction among students.
