papers.title: From Data to Decision-Making: A Review of Large Language Model Applications Across the Full Lifecycle of Geothermal Resource Development
papers.abstract: Geothermal resource development involves heterogeneous geological and engineering records, uncertain reservoir parameters, and decisions constrained by physical processes and safety requirements. This narrative and critical review examines how large language models (LLMs), including retrieval-augmented and tool-assisted systems, could support knowledge-intensive tasks throughout geothermal exploration, development, and operation. It distinguishes direct geothermal evidence from empirical evaluations in adjacent fields and from conceptual proposals; results from petroleum engineering, mineral exploration, and broader energy systems are not treated as proof of geothermal performance. Peer-reviewed studies demonstrate useful capabilities in technical document extraction, domain question answering, knowledge-graph reasoning, and interactions with scientific software, but direct geothermal engineering validation remains limited. For reservoir inversion, drilling-risk warning, and design optimization, quantitative assessment must rely on measured data and validated physical or numerical models, with LLMs acting as auditable interfaces and information-integration tools. The review proposes a task-specific benchmark framework and examines cross-domain transfer, multimodal alignment, knowledge-graph and retrieval collaboration, uncertainty quantification, and LLM–physical-model coupling. These frameworks are literature-informed proposals rather than implemented geothermal systems. Key priorities include independent geothermal test sets, expert-annotated reference answers, calibrated uncertainty, physics-based verification, and transparent reporting of model failure. The resulting synthesis identifies credible current applications and the evidence requirements for reliable future deployment.

papers.title: Direct Ink Writing of an Orthogonal Collagen-Based Membrane for Sutureless Corneal Repair.
papers.abstract: The native corneal stroma is composed of highly organized collagen lamellae with alternating orientations. However, reconstructing this complex architecture while avoiding suture-associated complications remains a major challenge in corneal repair. Herein, building on the previously established pseudo-polyrotaxane and collagen (PPR-COL) system, an orthogonally structured PPR-COL membrane fabricated via direct ink writing (DIW) was integrated with a bioadhesive layer composed of gelatin methacryloyl and oxidized hyaluronic acid for sutureless fixation. The concentration-dependent rheological behavior and printing performance of the PPR-COL inks were systematically investigated to determine the optimal formulation that balanced extrusion capability with structural fidelity. The chemical structure and morphology of the bioadhesive layer were characterized, and its maximum tissue adhesion strength reached 95.1 kPa. Subsequent in vitro experiments confirmed the cytocompatibility of the PPR-COL membrane and determined the optimal photo-crosslinking duration. In a rabbit lamellar keratoplasty model, the printed membrane combined with the bioadhesive fixation promoted the repair of the corneal epithelium and stroma within 28 days and maintained favorable outcomes throughout a 180-day follow-up period, as demonstrated by slit-lamp examination, optical coherence tomography, histological analysis, corneal topography, biomechanical assessment, and in vivo confocal microscopy. Collectively, this study presents an integrated strategy for the fabrication and sutureless fixation of collagen-based membranes, providing a potential approach for corneal stromal reconstruction. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: A bioinspired collagen-based corneal membrane was fabricated by direct ink writing using a previously established pseudopolyrotaxane-collagen bioink. The printed membrane reproduced the orthogonal lamellar architecture of the native corneal stroma, providing a structurally organized collagen-based substitute for corneal stromal repair. Moreover, an oxidized hyaluronic acid/GelMA bioadhesive interface was integrated with the printed membrane to achieve stable sutureless fixation to the host corneal bed. In vivo lamellar keratoplasty demonstrated favorable tissue integration, corneal reconstruction, and long-term biocompatibility. This work provides an integrated structural and interfacial design strategy for developing biomimetic collagen-based corneal substitutes and advancing minimally invasive corneal repair.

papers.title: Custom Triflange Acetabular Components in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: Survivorship, Clinical Outcomes and Risk Factors for Failure.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The objectives of this study were to assess survivorship, functional outcomes, radiographic osseointegration, complications, and risk factors for failure in revision total hip arthroplasty (THA) with custom triflange acetabular components (CTAC) at mid-term follow-up. METHODS: This study included 56 non-oncological patients who had advanced acetabular bone defects undergoing revision THAs using CTACs. Implant survivorship, the Oxford Hip Score (OHS), the Harris Hip Score (HHS), the University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) activity score, the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), the Forgotten Joint (FJS) Score, plain radiographic evidence of osseointegration, and any complications were recorded at the most recent follow-up. The mean follow-up time was 44.8 months (range, 13.7 to 63.4). RESULTS: Survivorship of the CTAC was 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 82.6 to 98.2) with CTAC revision for aseptic loosening as the end point. In total, five CTACs were revised: three for aseptic loosening and two for prosthetic joint infections. The median OHS improved from 12 (interquartile range(IQR), 10 to 14) preoperatively to 36 (IQR, 34 to 38) at final follow-up (P < 0.001). The median HHS was 64 (IQR, 60 to 72), the median UCLA score was 6 (IQR, 5 to 7), the median WOMAC score was 34 (IQR, 40 to 26), and the median FJS was 28 (IQR, 22 to 34) at final follow-up. Radiographic osseointegration at the bone-implant interface was observed in 42 patients (75.0%). Risk factors for radiographic failure included more than four previous hip operations (P < 0.001) and greater than two-thirds of ischial osteolysis (P < 0.001). DISCUSSION: The reconstruction of advanced acetabular bone defects with CTACs is associated with excellent component survivorship, low risk of aseptic loosening, satisfactory functional outcomes, and good radiographic evidence of osseointegration. Multiple previous hip operations and extensive ischial osteolysis were associated with increased risk of radiographic failure.

papers.title: Osteomodulatory potential of green-synthesized SA-ZnO/PVA coatings on Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: Bone fractures and skeletal injuries resulting from trauma, accidents, or diseases remain a major global health concern, often requiring surgical intervention with orthopedic implants. Titanium-alloys, are commonly employed due to superior structural properties and excellent corrosion resistance. However, these implants lack antibacterial activity and may release toxic ions, increasing the risk of infection, inflammation, and impaired bone healing. Surface modification using bioactive coatings is a promising strategy to overcome these limitations. In this study, a green-synthesized Saraca asoca mediated zinc oxide and polyvinyl alcohol (SA-ZnO/PVA) nanocomposite coating was applied to Ti-6Al-4V substrates, followed by characterization and evaluation of their biological performance. The coated and uncoated substrates were evaluated for mechanical strength, surface topography, and in vitro biological performance using MC3T3-E1 osteoblast cells, including cell viability, migration, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and osteogenic differentiation. In vivo studies in a rat femur defect model assessed the potential of coating for bone regeneration, osseointegration, systemic inflammatory response, and visceral organ toxicity. The SA-ZnO/PVA coated substrates maintained mechanical integrity, supported higher osteoblast viability with lower ROS levels compared to uncoated titanium. Coated substrates also promoted faster cell migration, enhanced early osteogenic differentiation, and improved bone formation. These findings suggest that SA-ZnO/PVA coating enhances the antibacterial, cytocompatibility, and hemocompatible properties of Ti-6Al-4V alloy, promoting faster and safer bone healing. The study demonstrates that green synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles blended PVA coatings effectively enhances the surface properties of Ti-6Al-4V, making it a suitable for orthopedic implant applications.

papers.title: Adaptive federated data pipeline optimization for low-latency AI inference in distributed edge computing environments
papers.abstract: Federated edge frameworks assume static pipelines, but real latency comes from ingestion, preprocessing, and aggregation delays. To address this shortcoming in federated edge intelligence, we propose Adaptive Federated Pipeline Optimization (AFPO). The framework jointly optimizes pipeline-stage allocation, federated aggregation, and model compression under dynamic edge conditions. We present a 3-layer architecture (sensing tier, federation tier, inference tier) that uses a Reinforcement Learning-based scheduler to assign pipeline stages based on real-time resource telemetry, a latency-aware aggregation mechanism that reduces the effects of stragglers, and an Adaptive Compression Module that dynamically adapts quantization and pruning based on latency feedback. We demonstrate that this problem is strongly NP-hard and establish that AFPO will converge under non-IID data, time-varying network conditions, and deadline-based straggler dropping. AFPO was evaluated empirically on the CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST image-classification benchmarks. Compared to the baselines of FedAvg and FedProx, which are tailored to training, it cuts down inference latency by 35.7%, decreases the communication overhead by 40.6%, and boosts classification accuracy by 5.08 percentage points. This accuracy advantage is specific to those baselines. Against inference-optimized baselines reconstructed in the same simulation environment, AFPO attains the lowest latency and communication cost but slightly lower accuracy (0.896 versus 0.905–0.910). It therefore trades a small amount of accuracy for improved latency and communication efficiency. The RL-based scheduler is trained using a policy-gradient approach. The latency and communication-efficiency enhancements over rule-based, resource-aware, partition-based, and early-exit scheduling are statistically significant across eight random seeds with 95% confidence intervals. Significance applies to three non-IID severities, two network regimes and a second synthetic workload profile. For the image-classification workloads evaluated here, AFPO offers an effective approach to latency-aware federated edge intelligence in Internet of Things and autonomous systems applications.

papers.title: Filter-Coupled Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Regression for S–N Curve Prediction of Injection-Molded Short Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Thermoplastics
papers.abstract: Predicting the fatigue behavior of injection-moulded short glass-fiber-reinforced thermoplastics is hindered by the large, irreducible scatter of fatigue data and by the strong dependence of the response on the moulding conditions, which conventional point-estimate models neither reproduce nor quantify. This study presents a physics-informed heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression model (Pi-HGPR) that reconstructs the S–N curve of a given processing condition by predicting the fatigue stress amplitude as a function of the number of cycles, the injection temperature, the packing pressure, the specimen orientation, and the stress ratio, and that returns a 95% prediction band rather than a single value. The model combines a damage process-type physical mean, an anisotropic Matérn 5/2 covariance with Automatic Relevance Determination, and a local dispersion filter coupled to the process likelihood, which makes the noise level input-dependent. Trained on S–N curves compiled from the literature and assessed under two out-of-fold validation protocols (point-wise interpolation and leave-condition-out extrapolation), the model reaches a coefficient of determination of R2=0.839 in interpolation and R2=0.649 in leave-condition-out extrapolation, outperforming Random Forest and gradient-boosting baselines in both regimes, with a global empirical coverage of the prediction band of 92.9% and 86.2%, respectively, slightly below its nominal value and lower (76–81%) in sparsely sampled regions of the processing space. Automatic Relevance Determination identifies the packing pressure and the injection temperature as the most influential inputs, ahead of the stress ratio and the specimen orientation. Framing the task as predicting the stress amplitude along the low-scatter direction of the S–N field, and incorporating an input-dependent uncertainty, yields an accurate model within the tested processing window and provides reliable extrapolation limits governed by experimental data coverage rather than the learner.

papers.title: Harnessing additive manufacturing to architect hierarchical (TiB + Y 2 O 3 ) nanodispersions for exceptional strengthening of near-α titanium alloy
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables trace microalloying to form hierarchical (TiB + Y2O3) nanodispersions in near-α TA15 alloy: a quasi-continuous TiB network along primary-β grain boundaries plus intragranular Y2O3 nanoparticles. Despite totalling only 0.35 vol% reinforcements, this LPBF-architected structure achieves >10% strength gain at room temperature and, notably, 15% gain at 500°C while retaining comparable ductility — surpassing conventional composites that need an order-of-magnitude more reinforcements. This enhanced performance originates from synergistic strengthening mechanisms enabled by the thermally stable hierarchical nanodispersions. Therefore, precursor-assisted LPBF microalloying provides a useful strategy for designing high-strength near-α titanium alloys with minimal nominal reinforcement addition after process-window optimisation.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Framework for Robust Coffee Leaf Nutrient Deficiency Classification Under Simulated Field-Like Conditions
papers.abstract: Early identification of nutrient deficiencies is essential for maintaining coffee yield, improving bean quality, and supporting sustainable agricultural practices. Visual diagnosis under field conditions is often subjective, whereas laboratory-based analyses are time-consuming, costly, and impractical for routine monitoring. This study presents an explainable artificial intelligence framework for automated classification of coffee leaf nutrient deficiencies using the CoLeaf-DB dataset. The proposed framework identifies eight individual mineral deficiencies, a multiple-deficiency class, and healthy leaves. A comprehensive comparative analysis was conducted by evaluating representative classical machine learning and deep learning models under both controlled conditions and synthetically generated field-like conditions. To enhance model robustness, leaf segmentation, randomized background generation, and photometric augmentation were incorporated into the training pipeline to approximate selected sources of visual variability encountered during field image acquisition. Experimental results demonstrated that the Support Vector Machine achieved the highest classification performance, with accuracies of 74.9% and 75.3% on the clean and simulated field-like test sets, respectively. Among the remaining models, the Multi-Layer Perceptron and XGBoost also achieved competitive simulated field-like accuracies of 73.7% and 73.3%, respectively. Transfer learning substantially improved ResNet50 performance, increasing accuracy from 67.1% under scratch training to 71.4% with transfer learning on the clean dataset and from 62.4% to 70.2% under simulated field-like conditions. Illustrative Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP analyses of a representative potassium-deficiency example showed that the examined prediction was associated with chlorotic and necrotic leaf regions rather than the surrounding background. The proposed framework combines predictive modelling with interpretable decision analysis and provides a comparative basis for automated coffee leaf nutrient-deficiency classification; however, the multiple-deficiency class showed very limited diagnostic performance (MCC = 0.087, sensitivity = 0.095, and F1-score = 0.129), indicating that the present framework is substantially less reliable for simultaneous deficiencies than for individual nutrient-deficiency classes. An explainable AI framework was developed for robust coffee leaf nutrient deficiency classification. Support Vector Machine achieved the highest accuracies of 74.9% and 75.3% under clean and realistic conditions Transfer learning improved ResNet50 performance by 4.3 and 7.8 percentage points, respectively. Background randomization reduced shortcut learning and enhanced real-world model generalization. Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirmed biologically meaningful and transparent model decisions. The proposed framework supports reliable and explainable precision coffee nutrient management.

papers.title: An intelligent weighted adaptive regression process for reliable and uncertainty aware drought forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate drought forecasting enables the management and reduction of impacts on water resources and farming systems. Hence, this research introduces a hybrid machine learning model called the weighted adaptive regression process (WARP), based on Gaussian process regression, generalized ridge regression, an adaptive mechanism to dynamically update the kernel matrix, and a feature relevance mechanism to assign weights to input variables. The model is optimized using the enhanced multi-operator Runge-Kutta algorithm. Moreover, a novel feature selection method based on kernel ridge regression and permutation importance is developed, while an enhanced multi-variate variational mode decomposition is implemented to decompose the input variables. The WARP applied to forecast SPEI at three stations in Iran outperformed LSSVM, DRVFL, and CFNN with correlation coefficient of up to 0.99 and MaxAE of 0.49. The uncertainty analysis demonstrated lower uncertainty and narrower prediction intervals confirming WARP as a reliable and promising drought forecasting approach.

papers.title: Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation in Postoperative Recovery after Total Hip Arthroplasty and Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Synthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Lower limb arthroplasties, including total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA), are established surgical interventions for advanced degenerative joint diseases; however, patients frequently encounter persistent postoperative challenges such as pain, muscle weakness, restricted range of motion (ROM), impaired balance, and altered gait patterns. Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) is increasingly utilised in orthopaedic rehabilitation to address these neuromuscular deficits, extending beyond its conventional neurological scope. This narrative review evaluates and consolidates evidence on the efficacy of PNF-integrated rehabilitation regarding pain management, functional recovery, muscular strength, joint ROM, balance, and gait performance in adult patients undergoing THA and TKA. We conducted a comprehensive literature search across multiple electronic databases up to June 2026, screening studies that evaluated preoperative or postoperative PNF interventions against standard care, conventional physiotherapy, or no intervention. We synthesised ten studies, including randomised controlled trials, non-randomised comparative trials, and case reports. The pooled evidence indicates that incorporating PNF into lower limb arthroplasty rehabilitation accelerates functional recovery, enhances muscular strength, facilitates early improvements in active and passive joint ROM, sharpens static and dynamic balance, mitigates fall risk, and optimises spatiotemporal gait parameters compared with standard protocols alone. In conclusion, PNF represents a clinically valuable modality in post-arthroplasty musculoskeletal care, and clinicians should consider embedding individualised, supervised PNF protocols early into rehabilitation pathways to optimise functional independence and long-term quality of life.

papers.title: From Condition Assessment to Verified Intervention: A Dual-Loop Architecture for Intelligent Railway Infrastructure Operation and Maintenance
papers.abstract: Abstract Intelligent railway infrastructure operation and maintenance (O&M) must move beyond assessing current condition to managing how infrastructure changes under traffic, environmental exposure, and maintenance. Several gaps prevent this transition. Inspections can miss deterioration between visits or at unmonitored locations. Sensor measurements do not always reveal the underlying physical condition, network-level summaries can conceal local defects, and maintenance often begins only after problems become apparent. This Perspective proposes an engineering-oriented dual-loop architecture to connect condition assessment with verified action. Loop I combines sensing from in-service trains, uncertainty-aware condition estimation, and rule-constrained decision support to identify sites that need further investigation or maintenance. Loop II connects precise localization and controlled intervention with post-maintenance measurements to determine whether the intended change occurred. Cases from the Dazhun heavy-haul line and a kilometer-span high-speed railway bridge illustrate components that can be deployed and the connections that remain unresolved. This perspective outlines a staged research agenda focused on data alignment, uncertainty quantification, safety assurance, human authorization, transfer across railway lines, and learning from verified interventions. The proposed architecture provides a testable path from condition assessment to verified intervention.

papers.abstract: This study examines the relationship between constructivist pedagogical mediation and student retention in higher education, emphasizing STEAM programs in Costa Rica. Collaborative learning, problem- and project-based learning, design thinking, gamification, and educational technologies emerge as relevant mediation strategies, whose effectiveness depends on institutional support, teacher preparation, and student context. The scarcity of Costa Rican empirical studies, particularly in STEAM, highlights the need for local validation.

papers.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
papers.abstract: Actions that condition world models are highly heterogeneous, and thus existing action-conditioned world models are typically built for individual action types, fragmenting already limited action-annotated data across separate models. We introduce UniAction, a unified action-conditioning framework that represents any action as a sparse set of action elements, each with a discrete semantic identity and a continuous spatiotemporal grounding coordinate. By mapping these coordinates directly into the pretrained video model's native positional space, UniAction allows heterogeneous actions to condition a shared world model within the same spatiotemporal structure. We further introduce cardinality-calibrated attention to address the bias from differing action representation granularities. We evaluate UniAction on four representative action forms: force, camera control, hand pose, and robot pose. UniAction outperforms conditioning alternatives in action following, and a single jointly trained model surpasses the action-specific experts, showing that heterogeneous action data benefit from unified model and joint training.

papers.title: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
papers.abstract: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

papers.title: A Tutorial on Physics Constrained Machine Learning for Hybrid Modeling, Optimization, and Control
papers.abstract: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Step Transition Predictions: A Bellman Theory
papers.abstract: Multi-step predictions of future transition realizations can improve reinforcement learning, but their value remains difficult to quantify. Directly including these predictions in the state can lead to exponential state-space growth, making direct dynamic programming computationally expensive. We study discounted finite MDPs under a block-feedback protocol: at the start of each K-period block, the decision maker observes $K$-step probabilistic transition predictions for a subset of actions and adapts decisions to observed states within the block. We show that the optimal value satisfies a Bayesian Bellman equation on the original state space. This representation reveals that predictive information creates value by recursively changing the local order of maximization and expectation in the Bellman expansion. We formalize this effect through a Bellman--Jensen analysis and quantify the effects of prediction horizon, error, action coverage, and within-block feedback. We propose block-feedback Bayesian offline learning with online adaptation (BF--BOLA), a model-based algorithm for learning near-optimal policies, and establish upper and lower sample-complexity bounds that match up to logarithmic factors in the stated regimes. The results show that predictions can reduce transition learning to uncovered rows and that learning a near-optimal policy can require fewer prediction samples than estimating the Bayesian value function.

papers.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.

papers.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
papers.abstract: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.

papers.title: Semantic Representation for Agentic Self-Play in Automated Laboratories
papers.abstract: Navigating complex, high-dimensional biological search spaces necessitates scalable physical and computational intelligence to explore beyond local optima through iterative self-play across ideation, experimentation, and automation. Translating experimental designs into reliable physical execution remains bottlenecked by static laboratory automation and unmodeled physical variability. To address this, we introduce VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories, or VERID, a foundational infrastructure designed to bridge the gap between the high-level reasoning of artificial intelligence (AI) agents and complex, error-prone physical realities of wet labs. VERID is a persistent, high-fidelity semantic digital twin of the laboratory workcell that provides four core services: queryable introspection for agentic reasoning, time-compressed simulation for protocol validation, comprehensive trace persistence for a complete scientific record, and a framework for safe execution.   We present three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures to validate the optical and fluidic foundations of VERID. These studies demonstrate how VERID enables pre-emptive detection of critical errors in experimental protocols, stateful mid-run error recovery and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures. The simulation functions as a discrete accounting engine, allowing agents to safely and inexpensively explore experimental designs in silico and refine experimental strategies through iterative self-play. VERID also captures structured multimodal experimental data for downstream analysis, knowledge mining and agent training. We argue that this semantic layer is an essential prerequisite for deploying autonomous agents in the biochemical and biomedical sciences, ensuring data integrity, operational safety, and paving the way for tackling previously intractable grand challenges in biology.

papers.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection
papers.abstract: Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states. However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction. Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation. Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.

papers.title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
papers.abstract: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. Third, based on this assessment, single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters using the PINN. Liquid viscosity, bubble initial radius, liquid density, sound speed, and liquid pressure are estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all, consistent with the sensitivity analysis. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.

papers.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles
papers.abstract: Achieving accurate, real-time lane-keeping control during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads while ensuring robust vehicle stability is a critical challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, this study developed a robust offset-free model predictive control (OF-MPC) framework for vision-based autonomous vehicle lane-keeping. The regulation problem in this framework is solved using several algorithms. Numerical simulation results indicated that the interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itube-CILQR) algorithm outperformed solvers based on the standard Interior Point Optimizer (IPOPT) and Operator Splitting Quadratic Program (OSQP), achieving a mean computation time of less than 5 ms. The itube-CILQR algorithm was then used for vehicle control in vision-based lane-keeping experiments in a simulation environment to quantify the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception model (multitask UNet). This quantification was performed using the OF-MPC framework for traffic scenes that were not encountered during model training. Overall, the developed OF-MPC framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.

papers.title: Acquisition for Spherical-Linear Bayesian Optimization on the Cube
papers.abstract: Recent work demonstrated that executing Bayesian Optimization (BO) using simply a linear surrogate with a clever transformation is enough to approximate the performance of the standard Gaussian-Process (GP) based version on high-dimensional test functions. When the decision region is a sphere, this strategy admits rapid exact acquisition. However, it is the unit cube we encounter most often in the BO literature, and in this setting a standard approach, namely a multi-start quasi-Newton method, is employed for solving the acquisition subproblem. In this article, we will discuss a series of results, both positive and negative, regarding the complexity of global resolution of various acquisition subproblems over the unit cube. On the basis of this discussion, we will propose a new acquisition function which is globally optimizable using significantly less execution time than the incumbent approach while maintaining or improving performance. The resulting method is competitive with GP-based BO in terms of accuracy per evaluation, and is superior in terms of accuracy per walltime on black-boxes of low to moderate computational intensity.

papers.title: HGWM: Hierarchical Graph-Guided World Model for Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Graph Matching
papers.abstract: Zero-shot object navigation requires an embodied agent to choose where to search while retaining evidence from previous observations. HGWM couples an LLM-generated room-anchor prior with persistent spatial-semantic memory. A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Phase-dependent fusion combines these scores with an LLM direction recommendation before local action selection. On HM3D v0.1, the reported HGWM configuration achieves 62.6% success rate (SR) and 31.5% success weighted by path length (SPL), compared with 58.1% and 31.2% for WMNav. On MP3D, the corresponding values are 46.8% and 17.9%, compared with 45.4% and 17.2%. The results indicate higher success point estimates and modest path-efficiency gains. On HM3D v0.2, the full model obtains 74.4% SR and 31.9% SPL. Additional component ablations reduce SR by 0.9-2.3 percentage points and SPL by 0.6-1.5 points. These are author-reported aggregate measurements. The accompanying implementation repairs pass offline tests; episode-level rerun records are not available. Evaluation is confined to simulation.

papers.title: BAARC: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Partial Spectral Measurement to Full Reconstruction for Material Classification
papers.abstract: Spectroscopic instruments with limited wavenumber coverage require accurate scan positioning or multiple measurements to complete the material analysis. This often requires prerequisite knowledge about the material under diagnosis to measure the spectral regions with distinguishing peaks. In our study, we simulate a Bayesian Adaptive Acquisition with Reconstruction-driven Classification (BAARC) framework for Raman spectral measurements, using masked training to learn spectral features that dynamically drive laser channel selection until the material is identified. We present a jointly trained two-level framework that takes progressive partial measurements of small wavenumber patches across the complete spectral range and, at each step, first attempts to reconstruct the full spectra until the model uncertainty is low. Secondly, material classification is performed at each reconstruction step until stoppage. Uncertainty quantification during reconstruction steps helps determine the measurement position of our next patch, while combining it with classification uncertainty determines measurement termination. By closing the loop between hardware acquisition and deep probabilistic modeling, the proposed system minimizes physical measurement steps while maintaining both spectral fidelity and diagnostic accuracy. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves high-accuracy sample identification using only a fraction of full-spectrum channels, offering a scalable solution for real-time, high-throughput spectroscopic instruments.

papers.title: UniWorld: A Unified World Model for Real-Time Visual World Simulation
papers.abstract: Continuous visual world simulation requires coupling evolving scene geometry with temporally persistent appearance. We present UniWorld, a unified framework that integrates depth trajectories and reference appearance within a shared video generation model. The central design maintains visual and geometric histories on a common timeline. Noise-aligned overlapping continuation places generated history at the prescribed sampling noise level and commits only newly generated latents. Rolling depth latent state preserves the corresponding geometric controls, incrementally reads newly available geometry, and keeps the conditioning fixed within each sampling window. Together, these mechanisms ensure exact preservation of latent history while bounding the active depth state by the window size. We evaluate continuous generation, paired history interventions, and long-horizon behavior across diverse scene categories. The same generator supports estimated, native, and on-demand simulator depth, while cached and incremental execution paths produce bitwise-identical outputs. Appearance changes and geometric control branches operate through the same interface without modifying committed history. The measured steady-state DiT execution path achieves real-time generation throughput, demonstrating the efficiency of UniWorld for continuous visual world simulation.

papers.title: Graphs of Trajectory Bundles for Nonlinear Motion Planning
papers.abstract: We present the Graphs of Trajectory Bundles (GTB) method for motion planning of systems with nonlinear and black-box dynamics, combining sampling-based motion planning with trajectory optimization and graph search. Based on a graph-of-convex-sets decomposition of the workspace, GTB iteratively constructs a graph of trajectory bundles that captures the local dynamics of the system at any vertex. By solving a shortest-path problem on this graph, we find maximally dynamically feasible iterates that satisfy the system's dynamics in the limit and any constraints such as collision avoidance or additional safety or specification constraints by construction of the underlying graph. As a result, GTB can handle highly nonlinear, unstable, and even black-box dynamics with complex collision and specification constraints, making it a powerful tool for motion planning of complex systems.

papers.title: A domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase CO$_2$ sequestration with moving wells
papers.abstract: We present a domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase geological CO$_2$ storage with fixed and moving wells. The approach builds on a nonoverlapping Schur formulation of a conservative RT0--P0 discretization solved by a sequential pressure--transport algorithm. The distinctive feature of the formulation is that local reduced models are coupled through physically meaningful interface variables: pressure traces for the pressure solve and inflow saturation traces for the transport solve. To address moving wells, we introduce a well-aware strategy that combines source-response enrichment, HAPOD-based far-field compression, and hybrid full-order/reduced-order treatment of well and near-well subdomains. We also formulate conservation-oriented hyper-reduction rules where interface fluxes, boundary terms and source terms are protected. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness of the overall methodology.

papers.title: Empirically Calibrated Differential Games for Simulating Driver Interactions
papers.abstract: Game-theoretic models can resolve vehicle interactions without hand-written priority rules, but whether they describe human drivers once calibrated has rarely been tested. This study formulates a general-sum differential game of vehicle interactions at urban intersections, calibrates it to observed driving, and evaluates it on data not used for calibration. Each vehicle minimizes a cost that combines speed tracking, adherence to a map-derived lane route, control effort, gap keeping based on the intelligent driver model, a predictive conflict term, and a contact barrier, while perceiving the other vehicles with a delay. The game is solved with a feedback iterative linear-quadratic algorithm, and ten behavioral parameters per vehicle are calibrated by Bayesian optimization on trajectories recorded at four intersections in Washington, D.C. The calibrated game reproduces the trajectories of 819 vehicles with a mean position error of 1.00 m. When only each vehicle's route is known, as in a simulator, it is the most accurate of the compared models on 96 held-out vehicles (7.42 m), and ten-fold cross-validation shows that it is significantly more accurate than calibrated SUMO (by 3.61 m), an inverse reinforcement learning model (by 0.93 m), and independent and cooperative variants of the same model (by 0.33 and 0.32 m). The solutions, computed in 2.1 s for a typical interaction, are verified approximate equilibria. Finally, the conflict and steering weights, which the data do not identify, can be set from safety and comfort targets; together with a stiffer contact barrier, this removes the collisions that otherwise occur in 43% of tight closed-loop conflicts.

papers.title: ACWM-RM: A Reference-Free Reward Model from Complementary Mismatch Preferences
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has gained attention for improving action-conditioned world models (ACWMs), as it enables reward-driven optimization of visual quality (VQ) and action-following fidelity (AF) beyond flow-matching optimization. Realizing this potential requires reward signals that reliably rank videos by both VQ and AF. However, existing rewards capture only one dimension: metric-based rewards assess VQ but require ground-truth videos and do not directly assess AF, while inverse dynamics model (IDM) rewards assess AF without references but do not guarantee VQ. Moreover, IDMs, typically trained on real videos, may provide unreliable rewards for generated videos containing visual artifacts and physical inconsistencies. In this work, we introduce the Action and Video Mismatch Benchmark (AVM-Eval), comprising 67.2k pairs that evaluate how reliably IDMs assess AF on real and generated videos. We then propose ACWM-RM, a reward model that jointly assesses VQ and AF without ground-truth videos during reward computation. To train it, we first construct the Action and Video Mismatch Preference Dataset (AVM-Pref) with 506.3k pairs providing complementary supervision: action-mismatch pairs supervise AF, while video-mismatch pairs supervise VQ and expose the model to generated videos. We then pretrain an action-conditioned predictor on real videos to learn forward dynamics before jointly training it with a patch-weighted score head on AVM-Pref to transfer these dynamics to AF assessment on generated videos. Evaluation on AVM-Eval reveals the limited reliability of IDMs on generated videos, while downstream RL experiments show that ACWM-RM outperforms reward baselines in both criteria.

papers.title: $Ψ$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
papers.abstract: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce $Ψ$-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. These streams interleave images, text, and explicit representations of geometry and motion, all of which the model can generate and interpret through a shared token interface. $Ψ$-0.6 surpasses leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning, with further gains from reasoning through geometric intermediates. It also supports counterfactual simulation: generating and interpreting imagined scenes to determine, for example, whether moving an object would obstruct a pathway. Reinforcement learning from task feedback jointly optimizes the selection, generation, and use of intermediate representations, improving visual question-answering accuracy with gains that transfer to unseen benchmarks. $Ψ$-0.6 offers a path toward adaptive physical reasoning -- not only predicting the physical world but also choosing the representations through which to reason.

papers.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Behavior cloning for robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to the coverage of its training data, yet collecting diverse successful demonstrations remains costly. We study reinforcement learning (RL) not as a deployable controller, but as a data generator for downstream visuomotor imitation learning. Our key premise is that multiple successful solution modes cover a broader range of successful trajectories than repeatedly collecting a single narrow solution. We introduce DiscoDemo, which trains a privileged latent-conditioned RL generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective to discover diverse solutions while preserving task success. The trained generator produces multiple successful closed-loop behaviors, which are safety-filtered and exported as a static dataset for downstream imitation learning. Across four manipulation tasks, DiscoDemo produces broader successful-state coverage and improves downstream visuomotor policies in both simulation and the real world. Averaged across tasks, downstream success increases to 62% from 40% for the strongest baseline in simulation, and to 78% from 39% on the real robot, respectively. These results suggest that successful solution diversity improves imitation learning for a pretrained flow-matching VLA and remains complementary to corrective data collection. Project page: https://davian-robotics.github.io/DiscoDemo

papers.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based image generation models produce high-quality images but may generate harmful or policy-violating content, motivating machine unlearning (MU) to selectively remove target concepts while preserving general capabilities. However, existing MU approaches often struggle with the distributed and entangled nature of concept representations, leading to inefficient optimization and imprecise edits when applied through large-scale fine-tuning over full diffusion trajectories. To bridge this gap, we propose Concept Acupuncturist (ConceptACP), a novel MU framework that integrates interpretability-guided analysis with inference-free fine-tuning for efficient and precise concept removal. By establishing mappings between semantic concepts and cross-attention blocks in the U-Net denoiser and localizing the most concept-relevant block for targeted optimization, ConceptACP avoids full diffusion trajectory optimization, thereby improving fine-tuning efficiency. To mitigate concept entanglement, we propose a feature-level correction mechanism based on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), where SAE-derived sparse, semantically meaningful feature activations are manipulated to construct targeted correction signals, which are then projected back to the output space of the corresponding block and used as supervision for precise concept removal. Consequently, ConceptACP eliminates the need for external inference-time modules while achieving efficient and fine-grained unlearning. Instantiated on SDXL-Turbo, ConceptACP improves the forgetting success rate by 36.34 percentage points in the standard one-step generation setting on average over the best-performing baseline, while preserving image quality and prompt fidelity, and generalizes effectively across other Stable Diffusion backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eran-Xia/ConceptACP.

papers.title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

papers.title: PPO vs. SAC: A Comparative Study for Cooperative Motion Control of Dual-Arm Space Robots
papers.abstract: The growing population of orbital debris has intensified interest in active debris removal and on-orbit servicing, for which dual-arm space manipulators offer improved grasping stability and load distribution relative to single-arm systems. However, coordinating two manipulators under inter-arm collision avoidance, orientation alignment, and sensing uncertainty remains challenging. This paper develops a coordinated reinforcement learning framework for cooperative motion planning of a dual-arm space manipulator in a target-reaching task with inter-arm collision-avoidance constraints. A centralized state representation combines joint-space, end-effector, and target-relative information, while a multi-objective reward function promotes target-reaching accuracy, orientation alignment, motion smoothness, synchronized task completion, and collision avoidance. Within this framework, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) are compared as representative on-policy and off-policy algorithms, and the learned policies are further evaluated for generalization to previously unseen target configurations. Across five random seeds, SAC substantially outperforms PPO within the considered fixed-base simulation scenarios: it reaches an 80% success threshold in every seed (median 1.6M environment steps) whereas PPO does not reach it within a 4M-step budget, and it attains a higher mean success rate (78.6% versus 7.4%) with lower position and orientation errors and tighter bimanual synchronization. Both algorithms degrade on unseen boundary targets, but SAC retains most of its performance while PPO's collapses. The results also expose a failure mode of PPO: under the two-phase shaped reward, it tends to converge to a reward-loitering local optimum rather than committing to the precision task. This behavior highlights the sensitivity of on-policy learning to reward shaping.

papers.title: Residual stress in LPBF 316L specimens: equilibrium-consistent reconstruction from neutron diffraction measurements, size scaling, and texture effects
papers.abstract: In this study, residual stresses (RS) in laser powder bed fused (LPBF) 316L steel cylinders were investigated to characterize their spatial distributions and dependence on specimen dimensions. Neutron diffraction (ND) was used to measure internal lattice strains, with particular emphasis on determining a stress-free lattice spacing, d 0 required to reconstruct stress fields consistent with global mechanical equilibrium. The reconstruction procedure employed area-averaged values of d 0 and enforced integral force equilibrium by applying small strain corrections within the experimental uncertainty. Near-surface stresses, which are important for satisfying equilibrium, are difficult to evaluate in cylindrical specimens using a conventional rotational ND setup because of limited spatial resolution and surface curvature. Complementary ND sin 2 ψ measurements on an LPBF plate, with a minimum measurement depth of 0.15 mm, were therefore used to characterize the near-surface stresses and guide extrapolation of the cylinder stress profiles to the free surface. The reconstructed stress distributions were independently validated by a sectioning experiment, in which the ND-derived stress profiles accurately predicted the specimen deflection induced by cutting. The effects of crystallographic texture, grain morphology, and elastic anisotropy on RS evaluation were also assessed using EBSD-informed self-consistent calculations

papers.title: STRATEGI KEPALA SEKOLAH DALAM MENGINTERNALISASIKAN PROGRAM 7 KEBIASAAN ANAK INDONESIA HEBAT (STUDI KASUS UPTD SDN 010243 BINJAI SERBANGAN)
papers.abstract: This study aims to describe the principal’s strategies for internalizing the Seven Habits of Great Indonesian Children Program (P7KAIH), to identify the obstacles encountered, and to examine the solutions applied at UPTD SD Negeri 010243 Binjai Serbangan, Air Joman District, Asahan Regency. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed. Data were gathered through interviews, observations, and documentation involving the principal, classroom teachers, and students, then analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model and validated through technique triangulation. The findings show that the principal’s strategies consisted of collaborative program planning with teachers, socialization through meetings and pre-lesson briefings, guidance and coordination, and periodic monitoring and evaluation. The program was integrated into learning through literacy routines, motivation, active learning activities, and the strengthening of school culture. The main obstacle lay in the habit of loving learning, namely low motivation among some students, differences in learning ability, excessive mobile phone use, and limited learning support at home. The solutions included literacy activities before lessons, instructional media and ice-breaking, teaching modules adapted to students’ characteristics, rewards, personal approaches, and cooperation with parents. The principal’s strategies have worked well, yet the results are uneven, so the habit of loving learning still requires continuous guidance from the principal, teachers, parents, and students.

papers.title: Autonomous atomistic-continuum coupling through uncertainty-aware active learning
papers.abstract: We develop an uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling approach for coupling an atomistic kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) surface-chemistry solver with a continuum multi-species fluid dynamics solver across disparate physical length and time scales. The surrogate model predicts boundary mass fluxes for six species and their uncertainties, which the continuum solver monitors to automatically trigger additional KMC simulations when new training data are needed. This enables efficient multiscale coupling and maintains a user-specified level of accuracy. We demonstrate the approach for reactive halide-perovskite vapor deposition, which involves a multi-species vapor jet impinging on a reactive substrate. The KMC solver uses a DFT-calibrated energetics model that we construct as part of this work and provides net deposition and desorption rates for six species. With a conservative uncertainty threshold, the surrogate-coupled approach reproduces cumulative mass fluxes of the directly coupled approach with errors typically within 10-20%, while capturing the non-monotonic dependence of net deposition on species partial pressure. Importantly, the results show that detailed crystal structure need not be explicitly represented to predict quantities exchanged between atomistic and continuum solvers; species-resolved mass fluxes provide a sufficiently low-dimensional representation of the atomistic response. For this accuracy target, the autonomous online-learning approach reduces the number of required atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude relative to direct multiscale coupling.

papers.title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fréchet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fréchet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Loève expansion of the same truncation order.

papers.title: A Gaussian Process State Space Formulation for Materials Constitutive Modeling: Application to Quasi-brittle Materials
papers.abstract: Constitutive models for history-dependent, path-dependent materials typically encode this dependence in prescribed functional forms through internal variables such as damage or plastic strain that are phenomenological, model-dependent, and not directly observable. These rigid forms lack flexibility to match observations, make calibration potentially non-unique, and complicate uncertainty quantification. This paper develops a Gaussian-process state-space model (GP-SSM) that replaces the fixed form of the constitutive model with a flexible GP regression, and the prescribed internal variables with latent state variables learned directly from observable stress-strain histories. As a GP, the model is naturally endowed with a measure of uncertainty and can be constrained to satisfy physical principles. We demonstrate this framework for quasi-brittle materials under triaxial compression, where the latent variable evolution is driven by the current-state stress invariants and the increment of equivalent strain to reflect irreversible, pressure-sensitive history. A sparse multi-output GP then maps the latent state and current strain tensor to the six-component stress response, trained by variational sparse inference. The trained model is exported into Abaqus/Explicit through a user material subroutine. Four verification cases are reported: (1) offline rollout on validation and test histories; (2) a single element under changing confinement; (3) a frozen-memory unloading-reloading extension; and (4) a multi-element structural model compared against the Karagozian and Case Concrete (KCC) model. These results show that the learned state-space update reproduces held-out RVE-scale histories in closed-loop rollout, tracks evolving confinement, supports unloading without violating the irreversibility of the learned history state, and reproduces structural-level behavior consistent with KCC.

papers.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the solution of the drift-diffusion equations with errors comparable to traditional simulation software using advanced training techniques to solve problems beyond the well-behaved equilibrium regime. For this study, we specifically choose an abrupt PN-junction in both one and two dimensions that features extreme gradients of the carrier concentrations at the Ohmic contacts and an abrupt discontinuity in the doping profile. Using the proposed PINN architecture, we are able to retrieve accurate results for all observables under all bias conditions. Additionally, we apply the PINN solver towards the inverse problem of retrieving doping profiles directly from desired electric field distributions or electrostatic potentials under non-zero applied biases. Our work establishes a powerful PINNs-based approach for semiconductor device modeling with the ability to solve inverse problems under non-equilibrium conditions for microelectronics research and discovery.

papers.title: Reliability Analysis Method For Small Failure Probability Based On Adaptive Kriging And Directional Importance Sampling
papers.abstract: The reliability assessment of engineering problems often requires computationally expensive finite element analyses and involves small failure probabilities; therefore, the development of efficient reliability analysis methods is essential. In this paper, a reliability analysis method tailored for small failure probabilities, termed AK-DIS, is proposed by integrating directional importance sampling (DIS) with adaptive Kriging (AK). AK-DIS identifies the intersection points between the directional vectors and the current Kriging-predicted limit state surface as a candidate sample pool, thereby achieving a high computational efficiency. The sample with the greatest predictive uncertainty is then selected from this pool to update the Kriging model. After multiple iterations, the AK-DIS procedure converges, at which point the constructed Kriging surrogate can be employed as a substitute for the original performance function in reliability analysis. AK-DIS was evaluated through six examples, including nonlinear problems, multiple failure domains, highdimensional problem, and finite element models. The results demonstrate that, while maintaining computational accuracy, AK-DIS achieves a higher efficiency than existing methods.

papers.title: AI-assisted nondestructive phenotyping of sensory-related traits in modern legume breeding: From sensing technologies to a proposed framework for breeding-scale application
papers.abstract: Sensory-related traits such as texture, flavor, aroma and appearance strongly influence consumer acceptance of legumes, yet they remain difficult to phenotype at the scale required by modern breeding programs. Human sensory evaluation provides essential reference data but is labor-intensive, costly and impractical for screening thousands of genotypes. Nondestructive sensing technologies, including near-infrared and hyperspectral spectroscopy, machine vision, electronic noses and related platforms, can generate rapid, high-throughput measurements of chemical, structural and volatile attributes that serve as proxies for sensory quality. When combined with machine learning and deep learning, these measurements offer potential for predicting sensory-related phenotypes. However, most existing studies focus on post-harvest quality assessment or compositional characterization, and rigorous calibration and external validation against human sensory responses in diverse breeding populations remain limited. This review critically examines the current status of AI-assisted nondestructive phenotyping for sensory-related traits in legumes, evaluates the strengths and limitations of major sensing platforms for breeding-scale application, and clarifies the complementary role of instrumental methods relative to sensory panels. We then propose a practical framework that links standardized data acquisition, robust model validation, uncertainty quantification, data governance and decision-support integration to enable more efficient, consumer-oriented selection. The framework emphasizes transferable rather than universal models, cost-feasibility considerations and responsible deployment within existing breeding pipelines. Overall, AI-assisted nondestructive phenotyping is best viewed as an enabling component of data-driven legume breeding that can expand screening capacity while retaining targeted human sensory evaluation as the reference standard.

papers.title: A Simulation-Based Physics-Informed Framework for Sparse-Sensor Prediction of 4D-Printed Morphing Actuators
papers.abstract: Purpose This study presents a simulation-based physics-informed framework for sparse-sensor prediction of 4D-printed morphing actuators, focusing on reconstructing the underlying stimulus field and predicting actuator deformation. Design/methodology/approach A physics-informed neural network (PINN) reconstructs the spatiotemporal stimulus field from sparse observations while enforcing the governing diffusion equation and initial and boundary conditions. A finite-difference solution provides the primary numerical reference, with an independent Crank-Nicolson solution used for verification. A 30-member ensemble is used to estimate epistemic uncertainty, while heteroscedastic prediction accounts for aleatoric uncertainty from measurement noise. The framework is evaluated through hyperparameter optimization, ablation analysis, sensor-density and noise studies, temporal extrapolation, parameter sensitivity, and computational-cost assessment. Findings For the main 25-sensor case with 2% observation noise, actuator prediction achieves an RMSE of 0.0067, MAE of 0.0062, and R 2 of 0.9991, while field reconstruction achieves an RMSE of 0.0095, MAE of 0.0060, and R of 0.9990. The actuator predictions show 92.50% empirical 95% coverage, with mean epistemic and aleatoric standard deviations of 0.0021 and 0.0045, respectively. Across repeated sensor-density tests, the 25-sensor case gives the lowest mean RMSE of 0.0048 ± 0.0029. Temporal extrapolation beyond the training interval [Formula: see text] achieves an RMSE of 0.0015 and R 2 of 0.9998. Independent Crank-Nicolson verification gives R 2 values of 0.9990 for the field and 0.9986 for actuator deformation. Originality The study integrates sparse sensing, physics-informed reconstruction, actuator deformation prediction, separated epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, and robustness to sensor density and measurement noise within a unified computational framework. The results provide a quantitative simulation-based foundation for future development of physics-informed digital twins, while experimental validation, physical-to-virtual synchronization, and online updating remain important next steps.

papers.title: An Intelligent Cyber–Physical Framework for Electric Bus Batteries: Combining DQN Smart Charging with LSTM Digital Twins
papers.abstract: The operational reliability of electric buses depends heavily on the thermal stability and longevity of their battery packs. In urban public transit, highly dynamic driving cycles characterized by severe current surges during regenerative braking and prolonged constant-current charging phases induce massive localized thermal stress. Traditional battery management systems often fail to dynamically balance energy recovery with the physical constraints of cell matrices, leading to accelerated degradation and potential safety hazards. This paper proposes an integrated cyber–physical framework that merges intelligent control with advanced prognostic monitoring and predictive thermal management. The core of the control layer is a deep Q-network (DQN) agent designed for real-time smart charging and dynamic regenerative braking current limitation (smart derating). This control loop is tightly integrated with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network-based digital twin (DT) operating at the edge level to mirror complex electro-thermal dynamics and track the battery state of health (SOH). To ensure transparency and proactive thermal control, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy is implemented, utilizing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to map core heat generation and dynamically adjust for internal thermal lag. The predictive NMPC-xAI loop maintained cell temperatures within a tight, optimal envelope, preventing delayed under-cooling and reducing peak temperature fluctuations.

papers.title: Tailoring Nonlinear Vibrations in Doubly Curved TPMS Shells: Interplay of Porosity Grading, Curvature, and Geometric Parameters
papers.abstract: This study presents an analytical investigation into the nonlinear free vibration of doubly curved shells fabricated from triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) metamaterials with functionally graded porosity. Based on Kirchhoff–Love shell theory and Donnell's nonlinear kinematics, the governing equations are derived via Hamilton's principle and solved using the Galerkin method combined with the method of multiple scales (MMS) to obtain an explicit frequency–amplitude relationship. A systematic parametric analysis evaluates the synergistic effects of porosity distribution patterns (PD-A and PD-B), TPMS topologies (Primitive, Gyroid, IWP), shell curvatures (spherical, hyperbolic, elliptical), and key geometric parameters including relative mass ratio (M/ρh), aspect ratio (b/a), and thickness-to-span ratio (h/a). Results reveal that porosity grading direction critically governs nonlinear hardening: PD-B configurations (porous surfaces, dense core) elevate the nonlinear-to-linear frequency ratio (ω NL /ω L ) by 6–14% compared to PD-A at lower mass ratios, owing to an optimized stiffness-to-mass ratio. Shell curvature exerts dominant influence, following the hierarchy hyperbolic>elliptical>spherical, with hyperbolic curvature enhancing ω NL /ω L by up to 8.5%. Most remarkably, hyperbolic shells demonstrate complete insensitivity to thickness variations—a finding unprecedented in the literature—maintaining constant ω NL /ω L across h/a=0.01–0.04, while spherical and elliptical shells exhibit 7–12.5% variation. This hyperbolic anomaly arises from a geometric locking mechanism that decouples thickness effects from geometric hardening. Decreasing b/a from 1.00 to 0.55 enhances hardening by 3–5%, and the synergy between PD-B grading and low b/a yields maximum hardening exceeding 28%. In contrast, TPMS topology exerts negligible influence (<1.2%), allowing selection based on secondary functional requirements. This work establishes a rigorous analytical framework for the multi-objective design of lightweight TPMS shells, providing theoretical insights that could inform the design of lightweight structures for potential aerospace, automotive, and biomedical applications requiring tunable nonlinear dynamic performance.
